registry.name: app-shell
registry.title: App shell
registry.description: Sidebar + top nav + page layout scaffold for an internal app.

registry.name: ai-chat-shell
registry.title: AI chat shell
registry.description: Chat surface with transcript, composer, tool calls and a context rail.

registry.name: data-table
registry.title: Data table
registry.description: Filterable, sortable, paginated TanStack data table with toolbar.

registry.name: chart-frame-data
registry.title: ChartFrame + data table
registry.description: ChartFrame (expand / flip-to-table / download-CSV) wired to @elabs-ai/components-data: full TanStack DataTable on flip and downloadCsv on export.

registry.name: ai-chart
registry.title: AI chart in conversation
registry.description: Renders a model's chart tool-output inside an AI conversation — AutoChart (@elabs-ai/components-charts) composed with Tool/ToolOutput from @elabs-ai/components-ai. The canonical copy-owned home for @elabs-ai/components-ai + @elabs-ai/components-charts cross-sibling composition.

registry.name: flow-canvas
registry.title: Flow canvas
registry.description: Branded React Flow canvas with custom nodes, edges and controls.

registry.name: flow-builder
registry.title: Flow builder
registry.description: Workflow-builder canvas with a node palette, auto-layout, grouping, placeholder growth, insert-between, an inspector, and copy-own undo/redo + copy/paste.

registry.name: data-model-viewer-01
registry.title: Data model viewer
registry.description: An entity-relationship view of a database on the flow canvas: custom table nodes with a row per column (keys, nullability, personal data), foreign keys as custom edges with crow’s-foot end marks that meet each table at the right row, a table list by schema with search and visibility, an all-columns / keys-only / names-only switch, auto-layout, and an inspector with columns, followable relations, indexes and a readable CREATE TABLE. Renders a plain DataModel object.

registry.name: agent-designer-01
registry.title: Agent designer
registry.description: A canvas for designing business agents: triggers, agents, routers, guardrails, human approvals and actions as the flow, and under each agent its equipment — model, skills, MCP servers with per-tool switches and ask-first, knowledge and memory — on square ports with dashed links. A searchable palette (drag, or click to equip the selected agent), an inspector form per node kind, design checks that point at the node they are about, a simulated test run that pauses at approvals, undo/redo and auto-layout. Three sample designs: support resolution, invoice processing, lead qualification. Plain data in, no runtime.

registry.name: marketing-hero
registry.title: Marketing hero
registry.description: Landing hero section with eyebrow, headline, CTAs and logo strip.

registry.name: code-workspace
registry.title: Code workspace
registry.description: Multi-file Monaco code editor with brand-ui tabs and token theming (wire @elabs-ai/components-editor/monaco-environment once at the app entry).

registry.name: sidebar-02
registry.title: App shell — dashboard inset
registry.description: The classic left-sidebar dashboard: a collapsible-icon nav rail with a tenant switcher and nav groups beside a floating inset surface carrying a metric row, a revenue trend and an overnight activity feed. Skip link, one main landmark, active-route indicator and command trigger included.

registry.name: sidebar-04
registry.title: App shell — mail
registry.description: Three-zone mail shell: the collapsible icon rail, a searchable message list, and a reading pane sharing one floating inset surface. A variation on the dashboard shell, not a separate idea; below md the two content zones become a drill-down.

registry.name: sidebar-05
registry.title: App shell — dual rail
registry.description: Two navigation levels plus a summoned third surface: a permanent 56px icon rail picks the area, a collapsible second panel lists that area's sections, and the floating inset carries the settings screen. A resizable right-hand SideDock holds the change history — a column above 1100px, an overlay below it. The icon rail is deliberately not a Sidebar, so it survives every breakpoint while the section panel becomes a sheet.

registry.name: stat-card-parts
registry.title: Stat Card — shared parts
registry.description: The pieces every stat-card block shares: the edge-to-edge chart bleed wrapper, the chart-hover→value/label/trend bridge, and the tokenized trend badge. Installed once and reused by the stat-card blocks rather than copied into each.

registry.name: stat-card-area-01
registry.title: Stat Card — Area
registry.description: KPI stat card with a live area chart sparkline, hover-driven value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

registry.name: stat-card-line-01
registry.title: Stat Card — Line
registry.description: KPI stat card with an inline line chart, hover-driven value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

registry.name: stat-card-choropleth-01
registry.title: Stat Card — Choropleth Map
registry.description: KPI stat card with a choropleth world-map chart, hover-driven country value/label updates, and a tokenized trend badge.

registry.name: stat-cards-01
registry.title: Stat Cards — elevated KPI tiles
registry.description: Elevated KPI tiles beyond a flat number: MetricCard + inline Sparkline (bar or line, coloured by a --chart-* token), a goal/progress tile, and a this-vs-last comparison tile.

registry.name: chart-card-kpi-01
registry.title: Chart Card — KPI header
registry.description: An elevated chart-in-a-card: a header with a headline KPI + delta + a segmented period control (ToggleGroup), a token-coloured AreaChart, and a footer breakdown legend. The period control re-renders the chart.

registry.name: stat-list-01
registry.title: Stat List — ranked list, leaderboard, activity feed
registry.description: Compact summary widgets: a ranked list with share bars + delta (Sales by country), a leaderboard (Top performers), and a transaction/activity feed with signed amounts.

registry.name: integration-grid-01
registry.title: Integration Grid
registry.description: A responsive grid of integration cards (icon + name + description + connect/manage action + connection status) under a page header with an Add action — the canonical ‘connect your tools’ surface. Logos are consumer-supplied (Lucide placeholders here).

registry.name: form-wizard-01
registry.title: Form Wizard — checkout flow
registry.description: A multi-step form with a horizontal numbered stepper (the Wizard primitive) — a checkout flow (Customer → Shipping → Payment → Review) with real fields, correct autocomplete/type hints, and a Descriptions review step.

registry.name: terminal-session-idle
registry.title: Terminal session (idle)
registry.description: A settled coding-agent console: launch banner, transcript, composer with mode/effort indicator, status bar. Nothing is running.

registry.name: terminal-session-mid-turn
registry.title: Terminal session (mid-turn)
registry.description: A coding-agent console under way: tool calls, a diff hunk, a working line with a stop affordance, a pending permission prompt, status bar.

registry.name: chart-editorial-hourglass
registry.title: Chart Editorial — Hourglass Stream
registry.description: A funnel redrawn as counted barcode strips (UnitStack) with trickle threads (DrawPath) narrowing between stages, plus stage-to-stage conversion callouts. One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L13 Hourglass Stream', built entirely from @elabs-ai/components-charts' marks layer.

registry.name: chart-editorial-patchwork
registry.title: Chart Editorial — Radial Patchwork
registry.description: Events on a 24 h clock face, density shown by overlaid translucent sectors (fill-opacity 0.07–0.16 — the one sanctioned use of transparency in this system) with rim ticks and a category legend. One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L10 Radial Patchwork'.

registry.name: chart-editorial-almanac
registry.title: Chart Editorial — Bubble Almanac
registry.description: A category × category matrix drawn as hand-irregular blob bubbles on ruled ledger paper, with a margin note calling out the busiest cell (PeakRing + Marginalia). One-off editorial composition adapted from lieflat-charts' 'L9 Bubble Almanac'.

registry.name: process-explorer-page
registry.title: Process explorer page
registry.description: A map-first process-mining workspace over an order-to-cash log: the six KPIs as one ribbon, every control in a toolbar so nothing floats over the map, and beside the map a panel of statistical insights — throughput distribution against the SLA, the slowest hand-overs, the weekly trend, box and violin plots by region and channel — plus variants as colour strips, the selected element and deviations. A dock holds the dotted chart, the performance spectrum, the workload heatmap and the case table; a replay animates every order as a token. One useProcessExplorer instance drives all of it, so no two panels can disagree.

registry.name: kpi-card-parts
registry.title: KPI Card — shared parts
registry.description: The pieces every KPI card block shares: a named-baseline comparison row (delta + arrow + sign, pp vs % handled explicitly), an on-track/at-risk/off-track status (icon + text, never colour alone), an as-of freshness footnote, Intl.* value/delta formatters, and the shared fictional 'Acme Logistics' Q3 dataset every block reads from. Installed once and reused by the KPI card blocks rather than copied into each.

registry.name: kpi-target-bullet-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — On target?
registry.description: "Am I on target?" — a grid of KPI cards, each a BulletChart (value against target, last year, and 2–3 qualitative bands) plus a named comparison row and an as-of footnote. A lower-is-better KPI states that its bands read best-to-worst in reverse.

registry.name: kpi-multi-baseline-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — Compared to what?
registry.description: "Compared to what?" — one wide card per KPI stacking three named baselines (target, last year, budget), each with a shared-scale dot strip so the same number's distance to every reference reads at a glance.

registry.name: kpi-pace-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — On pace?
registry.description: "Will I make it by period end?" — quarter-to-date Progress bars with a marker for the expected pace and a computed days-ahead/behind status, plus a Gauge card reading a rate KPI against its target and thresholds.

registry.name: kpi-trend-reference-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — Better or worse than normal?
registry.description: "Better or worse than normal?" — a 13-week Sparkline trend read against a target pace, last year, and a normal operating band, with a text legend spelling out the line styles so the encoding never rides on colour alone.

registry.name: infographic-scorecard-01
registry.title: Infographic Scorecard
registry.description: The Power BI-style scorecard, done with an honest baseline on every number: one row per KPI — actual, target, a signed delta, a BulletChart progress-to-target, a 13-week trend, and a named status — in a horizontally scrollable Table.

registry.name: kpi-forecast-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — Where will I land?
registry.description: "Where will I land?" — a linear run-rate projection to the end of the quarter: solid actual, dashed projection, a ±1σ confidence range that widens toward period end, a labelled target line and a today marker separating the two, with the projection method stated in words.

registry.name: kpi-hero-satellites-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — What is the headline?
registry.description: "What is the headline?" — one hero KPI (a big value, a named comparison vs target, a 13-week trend against last year) with three compact satellite KPIs beside it, each a value + signed delta vs target + a tiny trend, composed as one card with a single separation gesture.

registry.name: kpi-composition-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — What is it made of?
registry.description: "What is it made of?" — a 100%-stacked segmented bar per card (revenue by channel, shipments by region) plus a legend list that is the accessible source of truth: label, share, absolute value, and the share's own change vs last year in pp. Bar and legend share one order and a rank number so colour is never the only link between a segment and its row; shares under 3% merge into "Other".

registry.name: kpi-ratio-unit-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — How big is it?
registry.description: "How big is it in human terms?" — a rate restated as a small, countable fraction ("1 in 12 orders arrived late") via UnitChart, with the exact rate spelled out beneath the rounded headline and a comparison vs last year. Highlighted units use an accent fill against a neutral rest rather than hue alone.

registry.name: kpi-movers-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — What changed most?
registry.description: "What changed most?" — the top 3 risers and top 3 fallers in a ranked depot field (on-time delivery, revenue), each row stating its rank, how many places it moved, and a diverging mini bar from a shared, stated zero axis. Distinct from stat-list-01's single-snapshot share bars: this is about movement between two points in time.

registry.name: kpi-distribution-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — Is it consistent?
registry.description: "Is it consistent?" — an average hides the tail: a median headline next to p90/p95 read against a named SLA threshold, a box plot of the record-level distribution with the threshold drawn as a reference line, and the share past it stated in text.

registry.name: kpi-streak-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — How reliable is it?
registry.description: "How reliable is it?" — a ratio/streak headline over a 30-day strip of day cells, missed days marked by shape as well as colour, with the current and longest streaks and a comparison to the prior 30 days.

registry.name: infographic-variance-bridge-01
registry.title: Infographic — What drove the change?
registry.description: "What drove the change?" — a revenue bridge from last quarter's total to this quarter's, split into price, volume, mix, FX and other, built with WaterfallChart and a Leader callout on the one or two steps that actually explain the move. Steps sum exactly to the ending total; every step states its own sign in words, never colour alone.

registry.name: infographic-annotated-trend-01
registry.title: Infographic — What happened, and when?
registry.description: "What happened, and when?" — a 20-week LineChart whose events are declarative annotations anchored to the exact data point they explain, inside a ChartFrame that carries the finding, the method note, a byline and the source row. Under 480 px the notes become numbered markers with a key.

registry.name: kpi-status-threshold-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — Should I act?
registry.description: "Should I act?" — a status (icon + text, never colour alone) read against a visible on-track/at-risk/off-track threshold scale with today's value marked, plus how long the current status has held.

registry.name: infographic-cohort-retention-01
registry.title: Infographic — Do customers stay?
registry.description: "Do customers stay?" — a triangular cohort retention heatmap: one row per monthly signup cohort, one column per month since signup, shaded by the share still active. A cohort younger than N months draws an empty cell, never a fabricated zero. One cohort is called out with a peak ring and a stated, computed gap against its named peers.

registry.name: infographic-part-to-whole-01
registry.title: Infographic — Where does the money go?
registry.description: "Where does the money go?" — a two-level treemap of Q3 cost, category → sub-category, drawn in one neutral mono shade except for the single highlighted tile, outlined and named with a Leader + HaloText callout stating its share and the change from last quarter. Tile area is exactly proportional to cost.

registry.name: infographic-small-multiples-01
registry.title: Infographic — Which depot is the outlier?
registry.description: "Which depot is the outlier?" — twelve depots in a ChartMultiples grid, one 13-week line per panel on one shared y-axis so height compares directly, each panel title showing its latest reading (or the hovered week’s, synced across every panel), with the outlier ringed (PeakRing), thicker and glyphed while every other depot stays on a muted neutral.

registry.name: infographic-before-after-01
registry.title: Infographic — Who improved, who slipped?
registry.description: "Who improved, who slipped?" — a DumbbellChart slope chart of 6 depots, Q2 → Q3, with the biggest riser and biggest faller emphasised and every other depot on a shared muted line; direction is carried by the line's own slope, never colour alone.

registry.name: infographic-gap-to-benchmark-01
registry.title: Infographic — How far from the benchmark?
registry.description: "How far from the benchmark?" — a sorted DumbbellChart, one row per depot, hollow benchmark marker vs filled actual marker, worst gap first, with the widest gaps emphasised; the gap's sign correctly flips for a lower-is-better metric.

registry.name: agent-ops-parts
registry.title: Agent Ops — shared parts
registry.description: The pieces every agent-ops block shares: a provenance line (source · freshness) for any figure, a word-sized confidence meter, an evidence chip (the kind of document a derivation read), a countable evidence-strength meter ("|||| 4 of 5"), an actor avatar that tells copilot / agent / person apart by glyph, Intl.* money/count/relative-time formatters, and the shared fictional "Atlas" AI-ops dataset (Acme Logistics) every block reads from. Installed once and reused by the agent-ops blocks rather than copied into each.

registry.name: kpi-provenance-strip-01
registry.title: KPI Cards — Where does this number come from?
registry.description: "Where the business stands" — four headline figures on ONE surface, each with an inline signed delta and the line that earns the number its place: source and freshness ("ERP · 2 min ago", "Derived from 61 open orders · 06:02"). Peers separated by hairlines, no value without provenance; the delta is secondary (arrow + sign, never colour alone).

registry.name: insight-feed-01
registry.title: Insight Feed — What changed while you were away?
registry.description: The AI-ops briefing pattern: a numbered feed of things the copilot did or noticed — a one-sentence fact, a paragraph of why, the evidence it read, its confidence and two actions — with a conflict item that carries no confidence ("No verdict — a person decides"). Beside it, a "Needs a person" rail of what stopped and a "Derivation load" split of applied / sent to you / pinned by people.

registry.name: provenance-record-01
registry.title: Provenance Record — Where did each field come from?
registry.description: A record whose every field says where its value came from: derived (confidence meter + evidence kind), pinned (who and when — a pin out-ranks any derivation), conflict (two permitted sources disagree; nothing chosen) or empty ("No signal yet" — never a guess). Each state has its own glyph + text, and the footer counts the four so the reader knows how much of the record is machine-derived.

registry.name: score-explanation-01
registry.title: Score Explanation — Why is the score 91?
registry.description: A scored decision decomposed into its signals: one row per signal, a signed bar whose length is the contribution in points and whose direction is the sign — ink for positive, the warning rung for negative, each with a signed number so the sign never rides on colour. One shared zero-based scale; the footer states how many weaker signals were considered but not shown.

registry.name: spend-against-limit-01
registry.title: Spend Against Limit — How close is each agent to its ceiling?
registry.description: Every non-human spender on the card programme, sorted by share of ceiling: monospace agent id, autonomy band as a status badge (Auto / Review / Hold), a bar with the ceiling drawn as a vertical mark, the literal "$612 of $500", and Revoke. Over the ceiling paints the destructive rung and says so. Above it, three autonomy-band tiles total the envelopes per band.

registry.name: escalation-boundary-01
registry.title: Escalation Boundary — Where does autonomy end?
registry.description: The one dial an AI-ops product must put on screen: a stacked distribution bar of every decision by how well it was corroborated, with the evidence threshold drawn as a mark; the evidence ladder (countable tick meter, meaning, decisions, share, side); and three "If you move it" scenario cards that state the trade in the reader’s units (cleared share, queue delta, catches, reviews per catch) and MOVE the boundary when clicked.

registry.name: decision-record-01
registry.title: Decision Record — Why did the AI do that?
registry.description: Every AI action expanded into the reason it happened: what it did, what it looked at (named, openable evidence), what rule applied (the clause, monospace), how confident (or an honest "not applicable"), and how to reverse it. Below: the check list (confirmed / not confirmed) and what the copilot proposes — numbered, editable, nothing actioned until a person approves.

registry.name: audit-log-01
registry.title: Audit Log — Who did what, and did it apply?
registry.description: An append-only audit table whose actor column tells three authors apart by glyph — copilot, delegated agent, person — and whose result column is a status badge with an icon (Applied / Held / Stopped / Reverted), so a row still reads in greyscale. Monospace tabular timestamps; the action is one plain sentence with the number it wrote in it.

registry.name: agent-trace-waterfall-01
registry.title: Agent Trace — Where did the run spend its time, and where did it fail?
registry.description: An execution waterfall for one multi-agent run: a stat strip where every number carries its comparison (duration vs p95, retries, tokens in/out, cost vs workflow average, failed at), the charts package’s Gantt at sub-second granularity with one row per agent span nested under its caller, and a context-flow chain that shows the hop where a required field was dropped.

registry.name: finding-cards-01
registry.title: Finding Cards — What did the copilot find?
registry.description: Recoverable-spend findings as a row of cards: a status badge naming the kind, a one-line title, the recoverable figure as the only coloured number (kpi-sm), a two-sentence summary and a primary + secondary action, under a header that states the programme and the total the cards add up to. The primary action is what a person signs; the secondary always opens the evidence.

registry.name: verdict-side-by-side-01
registry.title: Verdict — Keep this, cancel that?
registry.description: A keep-vs-cancel verdict side by side: two cards on the success/destructive washes with annual cost, a segmented seat-utilisation Meter and the deciding facts; a one-line reading of the comparison; “If you cancel” as four consequence stats; “How the copilot knows” as a numbered evidence list; and the refusal — the copilot prepares everything, a person signs.

registry.name: handoff-inspector-01
registry.title: Handoff Inspector — Where was the context dropped?
registry.description: One edge of a multi-agent run: sender → a metric pill on the arrow (context size, latency, tokens, fields present of required) → receiver; a context-comparison table (sent vs expected, status badge per field) that shows the required field that was not sent; the payload size against the workflow baseline as a Meter with a marker; and the edge’s 24-hour health beside it.

registry.name: table-with-sparklines
registry.title: Table with sparklines
registry.description: A DataTable whose trend column renders the charts Sparkline — a target line, a fitted width and a spoken label per row. `@elabs-ai/components-data` may not import `@elabs-ai/components-charts`, so this composition is copy-owned rather than a `data` feature. For a plain in-cell trend that shares one scale down the column, `meta.visual: { kind: "sparkline" }` is lighter and needs no charts install.

registry.name: editorial-table
registry.title: Editorial table
registry.description: A published table rather than an app grid: a zero-based bar column on one shared range, a diverging heatmap column centred on zero with its own colour key, and a mini-columns column for the quarterly shape — all from `data`'s own cell layer, no charts install. `layout="auto"` flips it to a card list below 450 px on the same table instance, so the sort bar keeps working. Every visual keeps its value in the accessible tree.

registry.name: command-center-revenue-01
registry.title: Command Center — Revenue desk
registry.description: A revenue desk in one block: a MetricGrid of four headline numbers that each name their baseline and carry a 13-week Sparkline, a ComposedChart of weekly revenue with its trailing average against a labelled plan rule, a donut PieChart of the service-line mix, a BumpChart of which line is climbing, and the accounts that decide the quarter with a Meter each. Container-query layout, so it holds in a dashboard column and on a full page.

registry.name: analytics-dashboard-01
registry.title: Command Center — Analytics dashboard
registry.description: Analytics, scrolling and selection together on one retail use case: four KPIs, a monthly revenue LineChart with its average line, linear trend and a six-month seasonal forecast band (analytics[]), a 60-store BarChart ranking that scrolls with scrollbar="auto" and maxVisibleItems={16}, and a margin × revenue ScatterChart whose lasso (explicit confirm) drives the ranking and a selection-share KPI through createLocalSelectionDriver. Container-query layout, tokens only.

registry.name: incident-explorer-01
registry.title: Command Center — Incident explorer
registry.description: Two selection fields on one screen: an AreaChart of incidents per day whose time-axis range picks days, a horizontal BarChart of incidents by service whose click or axis range picks services, and a DataTable of the pager log that lists the intersection — with four KPIs (count, median time to resolve, severe share, still open) computed from the same rows. Both charts share ONE createLocalSelectionDriver (fields `day` and `service`) and paint their own field's states; severity is a StatusBadge with a glyph, so colour is never the only channel.

registry.name: energy-desk-01
registry.title: Command Center — Energy desk
registry.description: Two hourly series on one window: a LineChart of the spot price owns the navigator strip (scrollbar="miniChart", controlled window + onWindowChange) and an AreaChart of site consumption follows it through xDomain, with a 24-hour rolling mean and a one-sigma band from analytics[]. Preset buttons (24 h / 7 days / 30 days / All) jump the window; a range on the consumption chart's time axis picks a period, and the KPIs price it hour by hour — consumption × spot price — so the effective $/MWh the site pays sits beside the simple average.

registry.name: command-center-live-ops-01
registry.title: Command Center — Live ops wall
registry.description: An operations wall that moves: a LiveLineChart streaming one reading a second, three Gauge dials with their targets on the dial, a Timeline of what the on-call already knows, services sorted worst first with a Sparkline and a status badge each, and a HeatmapChart of when the load arrives. The headline is computed from the services; paused freezes the stream.

registry.name: geo-network-map-01
registry.title: Geo — Network map
registry.description: A network on the map it runs on: MapCanvas in globe projection with one MapArc per lane, its width bound to volume through a paint expression, hubs as MapMarkers with tooltips, and a panel that ranks the lanes with a Meter and calls out the late ones. Selecting a lane on the map or in the list dims the rest and redraws that arc heavier.

registry.name: plan-office-floor-01
registry.title: Plan — Office floor
registry.description: Which rooms are free on a floor, on the building's own plan rather than a world map: MapCanvas plan declares the extent in centimetres, rooms are polygons whose state rides the fill tone and the outline dash, MapPlanOverlay gives every room a real button for the keyboard, and MapPlanTable repeats the floor as words. Optionally lays the surveyor's drawing underneath as a plan-unit background picture.

registry.name: plan-factory-layout-01
registry.title: Plan — Factory layout
registry.description: A plant floor in metres where each machine cell carries its state four times over: the tone wash, a hatch texture generated on a canvas, the outline dash and the word in the legend and table. State rides feature properties and hover/selection ride feature-state, so the channels never collide, and the four states stay four states in greyscale.

registry.name: plan-seat-map-01
registry.title: Plan — Train seat map
registry.description: A reservation seat map on a plan of the train: three coaches of 64 seats in centimetres, 192 regions. The overlay runs in group mode — one button per coach, Enter to go in, Escape to come back out — with an option to show the direction of travel and the walk between coaches.

registry.name: infographic-journey-flow-01
registry.title: Infographic — Where do they drop off?
registry.description: "Where do they drop off?" — a SankeyChart from the channel a request came in on, through what happened to its quote, to how it ended, with a FunnelChart beside it that counts each step. The headline names the channel that loses the largest share of its own requests.

registry.name: infographic-profile-compare-01
registry.title: Infographic — How do the options compare?
registry.description: "How do the options compare?" — a RadarChart with one shape per option across five scored promises, beside a ParallelCoordinatesChart of the raw measures behind the scores. The headline names the strongest profile and the promise it is weakest on.

registry.name: infographic-dependency-web-01
registry.title: Infographic — What depends on what?
registry.description: "What depends on what?" — a platform's call graph as a NetworkChart (node size is traffic, colour is tier) beside the same services as a TreeChart of ownership. The headline counts inbound links and names the service most others lean on.

registry.name: command-center-launch-plan-01
registry.title: Command Center — Launch plan
registry.description: A launch on one screen: the Gantt carries the plan with summary rows, dependencies, a baseline under the task that slipped, a milestone and markers for today and go-live; selecting a task spells out its dates, baseline, what it waits for and its progress in a Descriptions panel. The headline counts the days left and the tasks past baseline.

registry.name: command-center-market-tape-01
registry.title: Command Center — Market tape
registry.description: A rate desk: a tape of lanes across the top with price, move and a 20-day Sparkline each, over a CandlestickChart of the index and a BarChart of daily volume. Every move carries an arrow and a sign as well as a colour; the chart title is computed from the first open and the last close.

registry.name: geo-fleet-tracker-01
registry.title: Geo — Fleet tracker
registry.description: A fleet where it is: each vehicle's planned route as a dashed MapRoute, the part already driven solid, the vehicle's MapMarker at the join and the depot marked; the list shows stops done on a Meter and minutes against plan, and selecting a vehicle fades the others.

registry.name: agent-run-review-01
registry.title: Agent run review
registry.description: One agent run, reviewable end to end: a Plan with its decision contract, an AgentTimeline whose last step follows your answer, a Tool call with arguments and result one click away, a ToolResultCard hosting the chart the run produced, TokenUsage in the header and an ApprovalCard for the one side effect that waits for a human. Reports the decision through onDecision and never performs it.

registry.name: workspace-shell
registry.title: Workspace shell
registry.description: The frame every full-screen template sits in: the flagship app shell with its data turned into props — navigation groups with badges, the signed-in user, the trail, top-bar actions and a summoned dock — plus a docked assistant with a briefing, suggested questions and a conversation. frame="container" renders the whole app inside a box.

registry.name: revenue-ops-page
registry.title: Template — Revenue operations
registry.description: An analytics workspace for revenue, finance and BI teams: the workspace shell with a summoned analyst, a page header whose period and region controls re-slice the charts and the pipeline, the revenue command center as the body, and a pipeline DataTable with a win-probability Meter, an activity Sparkline, a computed Stalled flag and row selection feeding a bulk action.

registry.name: control-tower-page
registry.title: Template — Logistics control tower
registry.description: The screen an operations team keeps open all day: a headline computed from the exceptions, the network and fleet map blocks behind tabs, and an exceptions DataTable sorted by the closest promise whose row click summons the dock with the shipment's Descriptions, the recommended next step and its journey as a Timeline. The controlled-dock master-detail pattern for the workspace shell.

registry.name: agent-ops-center-page
registry.title: Template — Agent operations center
registry.description: The control room for a fleet of AI agents: the agent-ops block family as one product across four tabs — insight feed, spend against limit and the escalation boundary; the trace waterfall and handoff inspector; a run review and a decision record; the audit log — with every block callback wired and the review count reflected in the navigation, the tab and the header.

registry.name: customer-360-page
registry.title: Template — Customer 360
registry.description: One account before the call: a record header, four MetricCards (one with a commitment-marked Meter), usage against the contract as a LineChart with a labelled rule, a self-explaining health score, a RadarChart against peers, next actions completed in place, an activity Timeline and the people with the relationship gap stated in the title, plus a docked account brief.

registry.name: support-desk-page
registry.title: Template — Support desk
registry.description: Queue, conversation, context: a three-pane surface in the workspace shell laid out by container queries, a queue sorted by the promise that breaks first with a Meter per row, a conversation from the ai package's Message parts, a copilot draft grounded in named past tickets that you send or discard, and a context pane with the promise, the customer and what solved it before. Sending a reply restarts the clock and re-sorts the queue.

registry.name: incident-command-page
registry.title: Template — Incident command
registry.description: One live incident run from one screen: severity, impact and commander in the header, a streaming LiveLineChart of the error rate, an AreaChart with the SLO as a labelled rule, the dependency-web block for blast radius, and a runbook whose steps print into a Terminal, tick off, move a Meter and write the incident log. Steps run in order; the last one settles the stream and unlocks Resolve.

registry.name: market-desk-page
registry.title: Template — Market desk
registry.description: Watch the market, then act on it: the market-tape command center as the read side, a watchlist DataTable whose row click pre-fills the ticket, and a docked order ticket that is a real form — FieldRoot validation in the trader's terms, a NumberInput, a computed commitment checked against a limit, a review step before anything is placed, and a blotter that fills as orders go in.

registry.name: energy-operations-page
registry.title: Template — Energy operations
registry.description: A utility's site desk: the fleet's headline computed from eight industrial parks, the sites as a DataTable beside a MapCanvas whose markers say status in colour, shape and words, the energy-desk block re-reading the selected site's 120 days of meters, and a dock the selection summons — the contract, the open alarms with the runbook's response and an Acknowledge that steps the site down, and an analyst conversation whose first turn is a tool call over the meters. One selection state shared by table, map, desk and dock.

registry.name: security-operations-page
registry.title: Template — Security operations
registry.description: A security team's triage screen: the headline computed from the open queue (how many open, how many critical, the oldest), the alerts as a DataTable with a FilterBar over severity and source beside a MapCanvas that clusters the open alerts on the assets they fire from, and a dock the selection summons — the alert in Descriptions, its indicators, the alerts linked by the same user or host, and an analyst conversation whose first turn enriches the indicators and whose second waits for the approval to isolate the host. Contain and Close as benign move the row, the queue badge and the KPIs together, with an Undo in the toast. Below the queue the incident-explorer block reads the same sources over ninety days.

registry.name: developer-platform-page
registry.title: Template — Developer platform
registry.description: A delivery team's control room: the headline computed from today's runs (how many failed, whether main is green, when production last changed), the four DORA figures as MetricCards computed from 28 days of deploy history, the pipeline as a CanvasShell graph whose nodes take the selected run's stage results beside the run log in a Terminal — selecting a stage narrows the log to it — today's runs as a DataTable under a FilterBar over status and service, the audit-log block as the platform's trail, and a dock the selection summons: the run in Descriptions, the failing check and the change under test as a DiffEditor. Re-run failed stage re-queues the run, steps the sidebar badge down and appends an audit entry, with an Undo in the toast.

registry.name: auth-parts
registry.title: Auth parts
registry.description: What every sign-in screen in this registry shares: the AuthCard frame with the brand mark, a PasswordInput with a show/hide toggle, a PasswordStrength meter that names the rules still unmet, the email validator and the useAuthSubmit lifecycle (pending, server message, done).

registry.name: login-01
registry.title: Login
registry.description: Sign in with email and password plus brand-neutral other ways in. Field errors after the first attempt, a revealable password, a pending button and the server's answer as an alert; hands the values to onSubmit and never calls a server itself.

registry.name: login-02
registry.title: Login, split
registry.description: The sign-in form beside a brand panel painted with the primary pair. Container-query layout: the panel stands down when narrow.

registry.name: register-01
registry.title: Register
registry.description: Create an account: name, work email, a password with a strength meter that names the unmet rules, and explicit consent. Errors appear after the first attempt.

registry.name: forgot-password-01
registry.title: Forgot password
registry.description: Asks for the email and answers the same way whether or not the account exists; the confirmation names the address, the link's lifetime and the way back.

registry.name: reset-password-01
registry.title: Reset password
registry.description: Choose a new password: whose account, strength explained, the two entries compared, and an end state that says other sessions were signed out.

registry.name: two-factor-01
registry.title: Two-factor verification
registry.description: Six digits in one InputOTP that submits itself when full, a resend that counts down, and a recovery-code way out.

registry.name: verify-email-01
registry.title: Verify email
registry.description: The waiting room after sign-up: which address, what to do, a counting-down resend and the way back for a mistyped address.

registry.name: marketing-navbar-01
registry.title: Marketing — Navbar
registry.description: Site navigation: links inline when there is room and in a Sheet when there is not, aria-current on the active route, container-query layout.

registry.name: marketing-features-01
registry.title: Marketing — Features
registry.description: A SectionHeader plus a FeatureGrid of six outcome-led reasons.

registry.name: marketing-stats-01
registry.title: Marketing — Stats and logos
registry.description: A StatsBand of the numbers over a LogoStrip of who stands behind them.

registry.name: marketing-bento-01
registry.title: Marketing — Bento
registry.description: A BentoGrid of product proof where each tile shows the thing: a live AreaChart, a Meter, a Sparkline, status badges.

registry.name: marketing-pricing-01
registry.title: Marketing — Pricing
registry.description: Three plans named for who they are for, a billing toggle that recomputes every price, locale-aware currency and a featured plan marked in words.

registry.name: marketing-testimonials-01
registry.title: Marketing — Testimonials
registry.description: A masonry wall of quotes with name, role and a read-only Rating.

registry.name: marketing-faq-01
registry.title: Marketing — FAQ
registry.description: An Accordion of pre-sale questions beside a person to ask.

registry.name: marketing-cta-01
registry.title: Marketing — Call to action
registry.description: The closing ask: one primary action, one quieter alternative and what trying it costs.

registry.name: marketing-newsletter-01
registry.title: Marketing — Newsletter
registry.description: One field, a promise about frequency, validation and a confirmation that names the address.

registry.name: marketing-contact-01
registry.title: Marketing — Contact
registry.description: A short validated contact form with a topic Select, a personal confirmation and the other ways to reach the team.

registry.name: marketing-team-01
registry.title: Marketing — Team
registry.description: Names, roles and one line about each person; container-query columns.

registry.name: marketing-footer-01
registry.title: Marketing — Footer
registry.description: One-line positioning, three labelled nav columns and the legal row.

registry.name: settings-profile-01
registry.title: Settings — Profile
registry.description: A profile form with dirty tracking (the save bar appears only when something changed), validation on save, a counted bio and a danger zone behind a ConfirmDialog that names what is lost.

registry.name: settings-members-01
registry.title: Settings — Members
registry.description: Members with in-place role changes, a protected owner, an invite dialog that checks address, duplicates and seats, pending invites in the same list and a confirming remove.

registry.name: settings-notifications-01
registry.title: Settings — Notifications
registry.description: An events-by-channels matrix as a real table of Switches with full accessible names, locked cells that say why, and a count of events that reach you nowhere.

registry.name: settings-billing-01
registry.title: Settings — Billing
registry.description: Plan and renewal, usage Meters with an included-amount marker and overage in words, the card by its last four digits, and an invoices Table.

registry.name: empty-states-01
registry.title: Empty states
registry.description: Six empty and error states on StatePanel with the library's illustrations — first run, no results, an empty list that is good news, error, offline, no access — each saying what happened, whether anything is lost and the way out.

registry.name: onboarding-checklist-01
registry.title: Onboarding checklist
registry.description: A getting-started checklist that opens on the next step, says how long each takes, counts the minutes left on a Meter and ends with a closing state.

registry.name: todo-list-01
registry.title: Todo list
registry.description: Add with Enter, tick to complete, filter, clear completed; the header counts open and overdue tasks and every control names the task it acts on.

registry.name: kanban-board-01
registry.title: Kanban board
registry.description: Drag cards between columns or use each card's Move menu (keyboard, screen reader and touch), with a live-region announcement, per-column points and WIP-limit warnings in words.

registry.name: project-cards-01
registry.title: Project cards
registry.description: Projects as cards with progress against time on one Meter (marker = today), a derived health word, team avatars, due date and a counted state filter.

registry.name: commerce-parts
registry.title: Commerce parts
registry.description: The commerce blocks' shared vocabulary: a sample catalogue, a token-painted stand-in for product photography and one money formatter.

registry.name: product-grid-01
registry.title: Product grid
registry.description: A product listing with a category filter, sorting and cards that state markdowns and stock in words; sold-out products cannot be added.

registry.name: product-detail-01
registry.title: Product detail
registry.description: A product page with required options (the button names the missing one), a stock-capped quantity, delivery promises, a Rating and details in an Accordion.

registry.name: shopping-cart-01
registry.title: Shopping cart
registry.description: Stock-capped quantities, remove with undo, a discount code that answers either way, progress to free delivery on a Meter and totals that add up.

registry.name: checkout-01
registry.title: Checkout
registry.description: One-page checkout with autocomplete on every field, errors after the first attempt with focus moved to the first, a delivery RadioGroup that changes the total, and a slot for the payment provider's hosted card field.

registry.name: order-receipt-01
registry.title: Order receipt
registry.description: The confirmation page: order number, arrival, address, lines and what happens next as a Timeline.

registry.name: project-hub-page
registry.title: Template — Project hub
registry.description: Projects, the issue board, team load and members as one product: the workspace shell's navigation swaps views in place, the project-cards, kanban-board and settings-members blocks do the work, one dock explains the project or issue last opened, and every view reads the same issues so a move on the board changes the load, the overview and the navigation counts.

registry.name: agent-studio-page
registry.title: Template — Agent studio
registry.description: Where a business designs, equips and watches its agents, as one product: the workspace shell’s navigation swaps between every design with how it ran this week, the agent-designer block flush in the shell, the skill library and the MCP servers with “used by” derived from the designs, and the runs — a run opens in the dock with its steps, a paused one shows who it is waiting for, and a failed one opens its full trace (agent-trace-waterfall).

registry.name: chart-story-parts
registry.title: Chart story parts
registry.description: Shared by every chart-story block: the byline and source each figure signs with, and a seeded random for its fictional data.

registry.name: chart-story-bar-highlight-01
registry.title: Chart story: ranked bars, extremes highlighted
registry.description: A whole published figure: ranked horizontal bars on a track to 100 %, the three lowest and three highest rows in colour and the rest as grey context, a colour key above the plot, values inside the bars, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-bar-diverging-01
registry.title: Chart story: Diverging Bars
registry.description: A whole published figure: signed horizontal bars from a shared zero line, gains and losses in two colours keyed inside the description, signed value labels, a row note beside the outlier, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-bar-range-01
registry.title: Chart story: Range Bars
registry.description: A whole published figure: a range plot drawn with bar overlays — fastest to slowest, the middle half and a median tick per row on one shared axis, with its key above the plot, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-bar-stacked-mix-01
registry.title: Chart story: Stacked Among Plain Bars
registry.description: A whole published figure: one ranked list where the comparison rows are plain grey bars and the rows the story is about are stacked by component, with totals, a colour key, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-column-highlight-01
registry.title: Chart story: Highlighted Columns
registry.description: A whole published figure: grey context columns, the columns after the event in the accent colour with value labels, an arrowed note naming the event, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-column-diverging-01
registry.title: Chart story: Diverging Columns
registry.description: A whole published figure: columns above and below zero in two colours whose key is written into the description, a note on the low point, signed axis, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-line-highlight-01
registry.title: Chart story: Highlighted Lines
registry.description: A whole published figure: three named, coloured lines in front of a field of thin grey ones, names at the line ends, a note in the series colour, hover that lifts one line, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-line-projection-01
registry.title: Chart story: Lines With Projection
registry.description: A whole published figure: two crossing lines named at their ends, a shaded and labelled plan range in which the lines turn dashed, an arrowed note at the crossing, the colour key written into the description, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-line-events-01
registry.title: Chart story: Line With Events
registry.description: A whole published figure: one long weekly line over shaded peak seasons, dashed and dotted event lines, a target line, an arrowed note on the record low, a notes line that explains the shading, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-area-threshold-01
registry.title: Chart story: Area Against a Threshold
registry.description: A whole published figure: one line against a labelled threshold, the area between them filled in one colour below and another above, both sides named on the plot, a final-value note, method note, byline, linked source and Get the data.

registry.name: chart-story-line-seasons-01
registry.title: Chart story: Seasons as Dots and Lines
registry.description: A whole published figure: twenty seasons of daily readings as small dots coloured by decade, two average lines and the current year on top, the colour key carried by the title's own words, two notes on the cloud, method note, byline and linked source.

registry.name: chart-story-area-multiples-01
registry.title: Chart story: Area multiples
registry.description: Small-multiple area charts on one shared scale: a dotted network average behind every panel, the same shaded event, and the latest value in each panel title.

registry.name: chart-story-column-panels-01
registry.title: Chart story: Column panels with ranges
registry.description: Two column panels on one shared axis, with the promoter and detractor ranges of the scale shaded and named, and a computed share in each panel title.

registry.name: chart-story-dual-axis-01
registry.title: Chart story: Dual axis columns and line
registry.description: Columns on the left axis and a line on the right: axes coloured like their series, ticks aligned on shared gridlines, a shaded range, and a table tooltip.

registry.name: chart-story-pareto-01
registry.title: Chart story: Pareto
registry.description: A Pareto chart: sorted columns on the left axis and the labelled cumulative share on the right, with a computed headline.

registry.name: chart-story-donut-01
registry.title: Chart story: Donut with total
registry.description: A donut with the total in the hole, outside labels on leaders stating name and share, and small slices folded into Other.

registry.name: chart-story-pie-pair-01
registry.title: Chart story: Donuts then and now
registry.description: Two donuts under one shared colour key: the year in the hole, shares inside the slices, the same slice order in both.

registry.name: density-parts
registry.title: Density chart story parts
registry.description: Shared by the density-scatter chart stories: a seeded gaussian for their fictional data and the three selection tiles (count, share, mean) that total whatever is selected.

registry.name: chart-story-density-envelope-01
registry.title: Chart story: Flight-test envelope
registry.description: A flight-test envelope with every recorded position drawn: 200,000 fixes coloured by the zone of the operational design domain they fall in, solid where dense and single dots when you zoom in, with range and lasso selection totalled in three tiles.

registry.name: chart-story-density-wafer-01
registry.title: Chart story: Wafer map
registry.description: A wafer map of 150,000 probed dies coloured by test bin — a scratch and a hot spot become visible that the yield number hides — with lasso selection reporting the fail share and mean threshold voltage of the dies you circle.

registry.name: chart-story-density-fills-01
registry.title: Chart story: Fill latency
registry.description: Every order fill of a trading day, size against latency, with the SLA bands drawn on the latency axis; a range box over the block-trade tail or a drag along the axis reports the SLA share and mean slippage of that slice.

registry.name: chart-story-bubble-01
registry.title: Chart story: Bubble chart
registry.description: A bubble scatter on a log axis: size by head count, colour by region with a key, a dashed trend, selective point labels and a text annotation.

registry.name: chart-story-calendar-01
registry.title: Chart story: Calendar heatmap
registry.description: A calendar heatmap: weeks as columns, weekdays as rows, six sequential steps and a key that states each range.

registry.name: chart-story-dot-plot-01
registry.title: Chart story: Dot plot with range
registry.description: A dot plot: three dots per row joined by their range, a colour key, a top value axis and rows sorted by the headline value.

registry.name: chart-story-range-plot-01
registry.title: Chart story: Range plot with deltas
registry.description: A grouped range plot: hollow before, filled after, a signed delta per row, group headers and a top value axis.

registry.name: chart-story-arrow-plot-01
registry.title: Chart story: Arrow plot with target band
registry.description: An arrow plot: one arrow per row coloured by direction, percent deltas, a shaded target band and a computed headline.

registry.name: chart-story-waterfall-bridge-01
registry.title: Chart story: Waterfall bridge
registry.description: A revenue bridge: coloured increases and decreases between two totals, thin connectors, matched-colour labels and a callout on the step that matters.

registry.name: chart-story-waterfall-running-01
registry.title: Chart story: Waterfall with subtotals
registry.description: A horizontal waterfall: monthly steps, automatic quarterly subtotals, a closing total and a plot zoomed to the differences.

registry.name: chart-story-table-scorecard-01
registry.title: Chart story: Table with bars and sparklines
registry.description: A scorecard table: bar cells, a shaded heat column, category dots, sparklines with the last point emphasised and signed, coloured change.

registry.name: chart-story-heat-table-01
registry.title: Chart story: Heat table
registry.description: A heat table: a depot by weekday matrix with printed values, five sequential steps, a key that states each range and the maximum ringed.

registry.name: a2ui-parts

registry.name: a2ui-decision-01
registry.title: Agent asks for a decision
registry.description: An agent-designed approval screen (facts, the policy exception, a note, three ways out) rendered from A2UI data. Buttons name host actions; the app answers each one with the agent's next surface, and logs what it received.

registry.name: a2ui-insight-01
registry.title: Analytics answer with charts
registry.description: An A2UI answer composed by the agent: a headline, KPI tiles with sparklines, two AutoChart figures titled with their findings, the method and follow-up actions. A click on the chart drills into the next surface.

registry.name: a2ui-form-01
registry.title: Agent-built form
registry.description: A form the agent pre-filled from an alert: inputs, selects, radios, a slider and switches from the catalog. Every change is a named action the host folds into one draft, shown live; submit hands the draft over and the agent answers with a timeline.

registry.name: a2ui-streaming-01
registry.title: Streaming surface

registry.name: a2ui-guardrail-01

registry.name: a2ui-assistant-page

registry.name: document-parts
registry.title: Document block parts
registry.description: Shared by every document block: a fictional supplier data room (a contract, a policy, a quality report, a defect log, a batch record, an inspection log, a chart and a source file) as FileSource values.

registry.name: document-library-01
registry.title: Document library
registry.description: A data room with the file open beside the list: folders, a filter and one FileViewer that renders markdown, CSV, JSON, code, logs and images through lazily loaded adapters, with the viewer's own toolbar, find-in-document, pager and zoom.

registry.name: answer-with-sources-01
registry.title: Answer with sources
registry.description: An answer whose numbered citations open the source document at the quoted sentence: the viewer swaps files, locates the quote, scrolls to it and marks it — and says so when a cited passage is not in the file.

registry.name: document-review-01
registry.title: Document review

registry.name: media-parts
registry.title: Media block parts
registry.description: Shared by every media block: sample media synthesized inline — a silent clip standing in for a film or a recording, a WebVTT captions track, poster frames, cover art and product screenshots drawn as SVG in system colours — so the blocks render offline.

registry.name: customer-story-01
registry.title: Customer story
registry.description: A case study as a reading page: headline and lead, the customer’s film in the ui Video player, results as metric tiles, the numbered narrative with pull quotes beside a sticky fact sheet, a screenshot gallery with a lightbox, related stories and a call to action.

registry.name: podcast-player-01
registry.title: Podcast player
registry.description: A show’s episodes beside one player composed from the ui MediaPlayer parts — cover art, the waveform as scrubber, a bar with speed — plus clickable chapters and a transcript that follows playback; choosing an episode from the list starts it.

registry.name: media-gallery-01
registry.title: Media gallery

registry.name: video-gallery-01
registry.title: Video gallery
registry.description: A filterable grid of video tiles — poster, play mark, duration, title and date — that opens the chosen video in a dialog with the ui Video player (captions, keyboard, docked controls) and previous/next to move through the set.

templates.name: ai-assistant

templates.description: AI assistant template — the canonical full-screen AI assistant composition: app-shell nav, an immersive `ChatShell` (transcript scrolls behind a floating `Composer`, one centred reading column) and the `ContextPanel` right rail. templates.name: marketing
templates.title: Patterns/Templates/Starters/Marketing
templates.description: Marketing landing template — the canonical full-screen presales/landing composition: sticky nav + Hero + StatsBand + FeatureGrid + UseCaseCard row + LogoStrip + CTASection + footer (the standard section order). This story is the single source of truth: `pnpm gen` derives the consumer template source (`docs/playbooks/templates/marketing.tsx`) from it. Verify across both themes with globals=theme:<slug> (light | dark). The marketing package ships no icons by design (sections take `icon?: ReactNode` from the consumer), so this story passes inline currentColor glyphs — the same way a consumer would hand in Lucide / @elabs-ai/components-icons.

templates.name: object-detail-hub
templates.title: Patterns/Templates/Starters/Object Detail Hub
templates.description: Object Detail Hub — the master-detail screen the library was missing. The single most common enterprise screen: a list of objects on the left drives a rich DETAIL HUB on the right. It demonstrates the structural choices the enterprise rulebook insists on, so an end-user copies the right anatomy instead of dumping everything on one page or stacking detail *below* the list: • SplitPanel master-detail (list drives detail — never detail below list). • A detail hub = sticky SectionHeader (identity + status) + a ButtonGroup toolbar + Tabs for the object's sections (Overview / Activity / Settings). • Descriptions for the object's attributes; a related list for its children. • A high-value task (Run) promoted to its own focused Dialog surface. • A real empty state (StatePanel kind="empty") when nothing is selected. Compose-only from @elabs-ai/components-* primitives; semantic tokens only; reads in light AND dark. Verify with globals=theme:<slug>.

templates.name: process-explorer
templates.title: Patterns/Templates/Operations/Process Explorer
templates.description: Process explorer template — the canonical full-screen `process-explorer` archetype: a map-first process-mining workspace over one order-to-cash event log. - a slim header with the scope, and the six KPIs as ONE ribbon (`layout="inline"`), so the height of the screen belongs to the process map; - a toolbar that owns every control — metric layer, deviations, detail sliders, the active filters, layout direction, table twin — so nothing floats over the map; - the map on the left, top-down so the whole process fits a pane of any width, and beside it a panel of statistical insights (throughput distribution against the SLA, the slowest hand-overs, the weekly trend, box and violin plots by region and channel), the variants as colour strips, the selected element, and deviations; - a dock for the wide, time-based views — dotted chart, performance spectrum, workload heatmap, case table — that stays a tab strip until one of them is asked for. This story is the single source of truth: `pnpm gen` derives the consumer template source (`docs/playbooks/templates/process-explorer.tsx`) from it, and the copy-own registry block (`registry/blocks/process-explorer-page/`) mirrors it. One `useProcessExplorer` instance drives every panel, so the map, the chips, the KPIs, the variants and every chart always describe the same set of cases (Invariant F: filtering re-inks, it never removes). Remember `import "@xyflow/react/dist/style.css"` is wired in Storybook preview. Verify across every theme with globals=theme:<slug>.

templates.name: screen-states
templates.title: Patterns/Templates/Starters/Screen States
templates.description: Screen States — the full state grid the templates omit. `design-first` requires that empty, loading, error and first-run states are designed WITH the happy path, never retrofitted — yet every existing `Patterns/Templates/*` ships only a populated "Ready" variant. This scenario fixes that: ONE representative data screen (Customers), rendered across the complete state grid as separate stories, with the SAME chrome and the real state primitives wired in: • Ready     — populated Table (the happy path). • Loading   — Skeleton rows (never a bare spinner on a data screen). • Empty     — StatePanel kind="empty" after a filter returns nothing. • Error     — StatePanel kind="error" with a retry action (role="alert"). • FirstRun  — onboarding empty: illustration slot + one sentence + one CTA. Compose-only from @elabs-ai/components-* primitives; semantic tokens only; reads in every theme. Verify with globals=theme:<slug>.

templates.name: settings
templates.title: Patterns/Templates/Starters/Settings
templates.description: Settings template — the canonical full-screen settings composition (app-shell + Descriptions + Wizard). This story is the single source of truth: `pnpm gen` derives the consumer template source (`docs/playbooks/templates/settings.tsx`) from it. Verify across every theme with globals=theme:<slug>.

playbooks.intent: Chat-first surface rendering rich agent output (markdown, reasoning, tools, sources)
KPI overview screen — metrics, charts and records laid out in one screen
Tool-first table surface for browsing and operating on records
Node-and-edge canvas for editing a pipeline or workflow, with a selection inspector
Standalone pitch page — nav → hero → proof → capability → relevance → trust → ask
Explore a discovered process: map, variants, filters, event log, conformance and case drill-down in one screen
Multi-section settings portal — sectioned nav, a form per section, guarded destructive actions

cliVerbs.does: Lists every type an agent may emit in a surface — props with enums and defaults, required props, events (`on.click` → the host action), whether it takes children — or the full entry for one type.
Prints the A2UI surface v1 JSON Schema (draft 2020-12; also published as `@elabs-ai/components-ai/a2ui/schema.json`) — feed it to a structured-output mode.
Runs `validateA2uiSurface`: one `path code message` line per problem (unknown type/prop/event, enum value, missing required prop, children on a leaf); exit 1 when invalid.
Prints a small valid surface (Card → Grid of MetricCards → Button with an `on.click` action) to start from.

conversation.title: Conversation — the AI SDK UIMessage (the default)
conversation.summary: Render what the agent SAID: a transcript of turns. The agent produces an AI SDK UIMessage; @elabs-ai/components-ai renders it. ~the default for any chat.
conversation.modelAuthority: Vercel AI SDK — import type only (D6). brand-ui does NOT redefine UIMessage/ToolUIPart; the SDK is authoritative for their shape.
conversation.owns: brand-ui owns ONLY the projection: the tool-state→Status mapping, the role narrowing, the fields its components consume, and SourceListItem.

parts.note: A reasoning string; pass isStreaming to auto-open + show a duration.
A pre-rendered React-element `output` is deprecated — emit a JSON payload and render it with ToolResultCard.
brand-ui-owned grounding item — not an SDK source part.

conversation.wiring: Your app owns the runtime: useChat() (from `ai`, in YOUR app) produces messages: UIMessage[]; map each message's parts onto the components above. @elabs-ai/components-ai never calls the model.

jsxPreview.title: Ad-hoc JSX — JSXPreview (the escape hatch)
jsxPreview.summary: When the agent emits UI as a JSX markup STRING. Flexible but less safe — prefer A2UI (data, validated) for an agent-designed surface.
jsxPreview.streaming: When isStreaming, partial tags auto-close (completeJsxTag) and a parse error falls back to the last good render — emit progressively; don't worry about closing every tag per chunk.
jsxPreview.safety: Renders ONLY tags present in the `components` allow-list you pass — the app decides what is renderable. Never widen it to arbitrary tags.
jsxPreview.wiring: Pass the agent's JSX string to `<JSXPreview jsx={…} components={allowList} />`. The allow-list is yours.

a2ui.title: A2UI — an agent-DESIGNED surface (data, validated against the catalog)
a2ui.summary: The SAFE generative-UI path: the agent describes a screen as JSON — a tree of catalog types with props, children and `on.<event>` action bindings — brand-ui validates it against the catalog and renders it with the real components. No code, no className, no style in a surface.
a2ui.protocol: { "a2ui": "1", "title"?: string, "root": node } · node = string | { type, id?, props?, children?, on? }

props.surface: A2uiSurfaceSpec | string (JSON text, may be a streaming prefix)
props.catalog: A2uiCatalog? — defaults to uiCatalog; extend with createA2uiCatalog
props.onAction: (action: { name, payload? }, context: { event, value?, node, path }) => void

tooling: `brand-ui a2ui catalog [<Type>]` — the types, props, enums and events you may emit
`brand-ui a2ui schema` — JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for structured output
`brand-ui a2ui validate <file>` — every problem with its path; exit 1 when invalid
MCP tool `a2ui` with `{ verb: catalog|schema|validate|example }` on the hosted server
a2ui.streaming: Pass the JSON text as it arrives with isStreaming: the surface completes the partial document, draws every node that already validates and prunes the rest; nothing errors until the input settles.
a2ui.safety: Only catalog types render; every prop is checked against the type's schema (unknown props, enum values, required props); className/style/code never pass. Actions are names the HOST resolves in onAction — a surface cannot call anything.
a2ui.wiring: Read the catalog (`brand-ui a2ui catalog` or the MCP `a2ui` tool), emit the surface as a tool result or message part, validate it (`brand-ui a2ui validate`), render with `<A2uiSurface surface={…} onAction={…} />`. Charts: merge CHARTS_A2UI_BINDINGS + CHARTS_A2UI_CATALOG_SCHEMA from @elabs-ai/components-charts with createA2uiCatalog (AutoChart, ChartCard, MetricGrid, Sparkline, BulletChart, Gauge); apps add their own types the same way (a KPI block, a domain card).

donts: Don't expect @elabs-ai/components-ai to call your model, stream, or manage transport — it renders the result; your app owns the runtime (D5).
Don't paste a frozen system prompt from this contract — assemble tool defs / prompt fragments in YOUR app from the manifest + this block.
Don't emit tags outside the JSXPreview `components` allow-list.
Don't put className, style, JSX or code in an A2UI surface — it is data; a type or prop outside `brand-ui a2ui catalog` fails validation.
Don't reach for JSXPreview/generative UI just because there's a chatbox — a chat that shows messages is still Build-with.
Don't invent component props — verify via `brand-ui docs <Component>` or the Storybook MCP.

props.name: summary
props.description: The business summary line under the name (`text-meta`), not JSON.

props.name: status
props.description: The canonical execution status (closed 7-state enum). Drives the rail node AND the `StatusBadge`. `skipped` is the agent-step-only state with no SDK source (research 10 §B.1).

props.name: hideBadge
props.description: Drop the inline `StatusBadge` (the rail node still carries the status color). For quiet prose rails — e.g. the `ChainOfThought` alias — where a badge per step would shout.

props.name: children

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Fires when an option is selected — by click, or by ANY keyboard move within the radio group (Home/End/arrow keys select immediately, per the native/ARIA radiogroup pattern Radix implements; there is no separate "highlight vs commit" step). Reports the full resolved `ApprovalOption` plus whatever reason text is currently held by a sibling `ApprovalCardReason` — type a reason BEFORE choosing an option to have it included in this call.

props.description: @deprecated Ignored (legacy attribute); removed in the next major.

props.description: @deprecated Ignored (legacy attribute); removed in the next major.

props.description: @deprecated Ignored (legacy attribute); removed in the next major.

props.description: @deprecated Ignored (legacy attribute); removed in the next major.

props.name: levels
props.description: Normalized 0–1 amplitude samples for the CURRENT frame — one per bar (or per sample point for `variant="wave"`). Update this from your own analyser polling loop (or the opt-in `useAudioLevel` hook) on every frame you want reflected; the component never touches the microphone itself. Any length works — samples are resampled to `barCount`.

props.name: loading
props.description: No stream connected yet — renders the idle baseline instead of `levels`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `"bars"` (default) — a bar chart. `"wave"` — a filled envelope through the current samples. Both encode level as HEIGHT, never as hue alone.

props.name: sensitivity
props.description: Multiplies each level before clamping to [0, 1] — turn up for a quiet input.

props.name: barCount
props.description: Number of bars/points drawn.

props.name: silenceThreshold
props.description: Average level, 0–1, at/above which the status text reads "active".

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Visually-hidden text announced when the discretized level state changes. Defaults to a localized label ("No input detected" / "Microphone active" / …). Pass `null` when the consuming surface already renders its own live region, so assistive tech is not told twice.

props.name: transition
props.description: Override the default transition handed to descendant Motion components.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary line, e.g. "Good morning, Avery".

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Second line, rendered under `title` inside the same heading. Independent of `accent` — either may be passed alone.

props.name: accent
props.description: Phrase rendered in `text-primary-text` with a bold underline, appended after `subtitle` (or alone). The underline + weight is a NON-hue channel deliberately layered on top of the color — a monochrome theme's `--primary` can be a near-white "pen" by design, in which case the accent colour alone is indistinguishable from the surrounding `--foreground` headline text. The underline/weight keep the phrase legible as an accent in EVERY theme, not only the two where hue alone would carry it.

props.name: orb
props.description: Soft primary glow behind the headline. Default `true`; `false` for dense/embedded use.

props.name: level
props.description: Semantic heading level for `title`. Default `1` (a chat empty state is typically the only heading on the page). Override to `2`+ when ChatGreeting sits inside a page or route that already renders its own `<h1>` — `Heading` decouples `level` from `size`, so the visual display-scale rung stays put regardless of the level chosen.

props.name: children
props.description: Scrollable transcript — typically a <Conversation>.

props.name: composer
props.description: Floating composer — typically a <Composer> (the standard chat input). It floats, padded, over the bottom of the transcript, centred at `--chat-composer-column` (default `--container-3xl`) under a transcript column of `--chat-column` (default `--container-4xl`, read by `ConversationContent`); turns scroll up behind it and fade out.

props.name: header

props.name: aside

props.name: variant
props.description: Frame treatment (the transcript/composer layout is the same in both): - `"card"` (default) — a self-contained rounded, bordered chat card with a divider under the header. Use when the shell sits on a page among other content and needs its own frame. - `"bare"` — an immersive pane that fills its container with NO frame and no header divider. Use when the shell already lives inside a bounded region (an AppShell `SidebarInset`, a full-page workspace) so it doesn't draw a redundant second frame.

props.description: Soft-wrap long lines instead of scrolling horizontally. Use in narrow embeds (e.g. a side rail) so content is not silently clipped. Default: false.

props.name: renderPreview
props.description: Draw an asset's preview body yourself. The seam that lets this package show formats it cannot parse — a PDF, a spreadsheet, a video — without importing a domain sibling (`@elabs-ai/components-ai` and `@elabs-ai/components-viewer` are peers in the layer graph and may never import each other). The consuming app owns the edge: ```tsx <ContextPanelProvider renderPreview={(asset) => asset.source ? <FileViewer source={asset.source} /> : null } > ``` Return `null` to decline, and the built-in type-keyed rendering runs exactly as before — so an injection is additive, never a replacement.

props.name: label

props.name: isStreaming
props.description: The assistant response is still arriving (loading-states.md `isStreaming`). `role="log"` otherwise announces every incoming token to assistive tech as it streams in — deafening. While `true`, `aria-live` is suppressed (`"off"`) and `aria-busy` is set; once streaming ends, `aria-live` returns to `"polite"` so the settled content is what actually gets announced. @default false
