ParallelCoordinatesChart.purpose: Same entities across 3-6 mixed-unit dimensions: one hairline per entity threaded through per-axis-normalized vertical scales, so shape and crossing pattern reveal correlation across axes that share no common unit.

stateTokens.axis: var(--chart-foreground-muted) vertical hairline with end ticks (HairlineFloor style)
stateTokens.extremeLabel: var(--chart-foreground-muted) on a var(--chart-background) halo, axis feet only when showExtremes
stateTokens.heroLine: 2px, var(--chart-foreground) or the resolved palette ink, opacity 1 — drawn LAST so it sits on top
stateTokens.nonHeroLine: 0.65px hairline, seeded 0.5-0.8 opacity — a texture of many lines, not individually legible

antiPatterns: Fewer than 3 or more than 6 dimensions — below 3 a DumbbellChart (2) or MetricCard (1) reads better; above 6 the axes crowd and `resolveParallelDimensions` clamps to the first 6 with a console warning, silently dropping the rest.

Dimensions on wildly different natural scales with no explicit `domain` — each axis normalizes independently, so an unset domain just uses that dimension's own min/max, which is usually right; only override when you need a domain that isn't in the data (e.g. a known 0-100 ceiling).

Using `highlightKey` to try to promote MULTIPLE entities to hero status — only the first row a predicate matches (or the one literal id) is promoted; for comparing several entities at once, dim the rest via a different technique or fall back to small multiples.

Reaching for this when the entities do NOT share the same dimensions, or when there is only one entity — a single-entity profile across many metrics is a RadarChart (shared 0-100 radial scale) or a MetricGrid, not a parallel-coordinates plot.
dataShapes: many numeric dimensions compared across entities at once
ParallelCoordinatesChart.avoidWhen: more than about 2 entities need per-entity detail — use small-multiple radar

PeakRing.purpose: A dashed outline around the one mark that matters — the peak, the outlier, the cell the caption is about.

stateTokens.ink: dashed 2 3 at 0.8px in var(--chart-foreground) — emphasis carried by shape, never by hue

antiPatterns: Swapping the dash for a highlight hue — the ring exists because emphasis by SHAPE survives greyscale and a colour-blind reader (WCAG 1.4.1). Recolouring it throws away the only reason to reach for it.
Ringing three marks — the ring points at whatever the caption is about. A second ring halves the emphasis and a third deletes it.
Treating the ring as the statement — it is aria-hidden furniture that points; it says nothing. A peak worth ringing is worth writing in the caption or the summary.
Dashing a plotted mark elsewhere in the same chart — nothing that carries data is dashed here, and that is precisely what stops the ring being read as a series.

PieChart.purpose: Part-of-whole split across a handful of categories.
antiPatterns: More than ~5 slices — a bar chart compares better; a pie is not a ranking.
A pie for values that don't sum to a meaningful whole.
Identifying slices by color alone — put the label and value on or beside the slice.
dataShapes: parts of a whole across a few categories, read as proportions of the total
PieChart.avoidWhen: more than about 6 slices — use a bar or unit chart

QuietDot.purpose: The 0.9px pinprick that renders a measured null or zero, so an empty cell in a matrix is never a hole.

stateTokens.ink: var(--chart-foreground-muted) at radius 0.45 — the quietest mark in the system by construction

antiPatterns: Scattering it as decoration — it has ONE job, and it is the null/zero render. A pinprick that is not standing for an absent value teaches the reader that absence is noise.
Leaving a zero cell blank instead — blank reads identically to no data collected, to the grid ends here, and to a rendering bug. The dot says the cell was visited and the answer was nothing.

Assuming it distinguishes 0 from null — it says MEASURED, not which. Where the difference is load-bearing keep the dot for the zero, give the missing cell a hatch or an explicit gap, and say so in the legend.
Enlarging it so it is easier to see — an absence rendered at the weight of a value becomes a value.

RadarChart.purpose: Multi-metric profile comparison on a shared radial axis.
antiPatterns: Plotting metrics with different units on one radar — normalize first or the shape is meaningless.
Overlaying more than ~3 profiles — the filled areas occlude each other; use small multiples.
Relying on the filled area to be readable at low opacity — check the fill against every theme's canvas.
dataShapes: several measures per entity, compared as an overall shape rather than value by value
RadarChart.avoidWhen: more than about 8 spokes, or absolute magnitude matters more than the shape

RampLegend.purpose: The colour-scale key for a sequential or diverging chart: a continuous ramp with its low and high values.

RingChart.purpose: A single value as a filled ring (a progress or share reading) with the number in the centre.
dataShapes: one proportion against its maximum, read as a single ring
RingChart.avoidWhen: several categories matter — use a pie or unit chart

SankeyChart.purpose: Flow diagram — how quantity moves between stages or nodes.
antiPatterns: A Sankey for a simple two-column comparison — reach for a bar chart.
Raw colors on nodes/links — resolve the chart tokens so the dark theme reads correctly.
So many nodes that the labels collide — aggregate the tail into one 'other' node.
dataShapes: a weighted flow between named nodes, source to target
SankeyChart.avoidWhen: the nodes have no real flow between them — use a network chart

SankeyThreadLinks.purpose: SankeyChart mode="threads" per-record renderer — one polyline per row instead of one aggregate edge per node pair, for tracing an individual route (e.g. a shipment, a session) through several hops.

stateTokens.pin: click the fat hit-twin to pin a route

antiPatterns: Using mode="threads" for a small, low-cardinality flow — that's what the default aggregate SankeyLink is for.
Supplying `path` names that don't match any `SankeyNodeDatum.name` — the route silently falls back to source/target only.
Making the visible thread path itself interactive — pointer handling belongs on the fat, transparent hit-twin so overlapping routes don't fight for clicks.
Relying on keyboard focus reaching inside the <svg> — the keyboard path is the sibling ChartDatapointLayer, never a focusable SVG element.

ScatterChart.purpose: Point cloud for correlation between two continuous measures.
antiPatterns: Connecting the points — a line asserts a sequence a scatter does not have.
Plotting tens of thousands of raw points — past ~20k use DensityScatterChart (every point drawn, density as colour); below that, bin or sample.
Distinguishing groups by colour only at default opacity — overlapping marks collapse; add shape or facets.
dataShapes: two continuous measures per row — correlation, or the shape of a distribution
ScatterChart.avoidWhen: one axis is categorical — use a bar or dumbbell chart

Sparkline.purpose: Tiny, axis-less trend that lives inside a KPI tile or a table cell.
antiPatterns: Adding axes and tooltips to a Sparkline — if it needs them it is a LineChart.
A Sparkline as the only carrier of a number — pair it with the value (MetricCard).
Fixing its width in pixels — let the tile or cell own the box so it reflows.

TreeChart.purpose: Fixed-spacing, left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) orthogonal hierarchy diagram — every node the same visual weight, no sizes: 'who belongs to whom'.

stateTokens.linkStroke: var(--chart-grid), 1.4px — links are furniture, not data, whatever the palette
stateTokens.nodeMono: --chart-mono-1 … 7, indexed by DEPTH (the default) — every node at one depth shares one shade
stateTokens.nodeCategorical: one hue per top-level branch (a direct child of the root); the root itself stays var(--chart-mono-4), since it belongs to no branch
stateTokens.label: HaloText in the chart-value type role, placed before a leaf / after a branch on the growth axis; the halo punches from var(--chart-background)
stateTokens.collapsedPill: var(--chart-mono-3) fill, '+k' label — k is the count of leaves the pill hides
stateTokens.reveal: links draw depth by depth via DrawPath + stagger — every link into one depth shares a single reveal delay

antiPatterns: Reaching for TreeChart when the real question is 'how big is each part' — that is TreemapChart's job (leaf AREA proportional to value). TreeChart has no `value` field on TreeNode at all, on purpose: every node is the same visual weight, so it can only ever answer 'what contains what'.

Sizing or coloring a node by anything other than its DEPTH or top-level BRANCH — the two palettes are the only two encodings; a third meaning bolted onto node size or a per-leaf hue turns a membership diagram back into an unlabeled treemap.

Expecting the layout to shrink to fit its container — TreeChart lays out at FIXED node/level spacing (no ResizeObserver) precisely so it never shrinks; a tree bigger than its box scrolls inside ChartFrame instead of compressing into illegibility.

Using collapseDepth as an expand-on-click affordance — it is a static truncation (a '+k' pill with no interaction of its own); compose onDatapointClick to open a detail panel if the reader needs to reveal a hidden branch on demand.
dataShapes: a hierarchy read as a branching tree rather than as sized rectangles
TreeChart.avoidWhen: size, not structure, is the point — use a treemap

TreemapChart.purpose: Two-level squarified treemap — a hierarchy where area, not position, encodes value.

stateTokens.band: var(--chart-mono-2) — always neutral, even under palette: 'categorical', so grouping reads from the title band + gap alone, never from hue
stateTokens.leafMono: var(--chart-mono-4) — one shared shade for every leaf (the default)
stateTokens.leafCategorical: one hue per top-level group (≤ 4 groups, else falls back to mono)
stateTokens.label: HaloText: the band title renders in the chart-source type role, the leaf label in the chart-value type role (RM-019, both pinned to the meta size step); the halo punches from var(--chart-background)
stateTokens.focus: the drilldown zoom/back buttons carry the shared compound focus indicator (--ring plus the --ring-contour outline), shown only on keyboard focus

antiPatterns: Comparing a leaf's area against a leaf in a different group — area is only comparable WITHIN one parent's total; two leaves under different groups are fractions of different denominators, so their tile sizes are not commensurate across the group boundary.

Reaching for palette: 'categorical' to encode a second measure on top of area — the hue there still only labels the group a leaf already belongs to (structurally, via the band); asking it to carry an unrelated variable makes one channel do two jobs and defeats the mono default's greyscale-legible design.

Leaving a long tail of small leaves unmerged until tiles fall below labelMinArea — set otherThreshold before that happens (the unconditional 30-leaf cap is a backstop, not a substitute for tuning it); a treemap of unlabeled slivers reads as noise, not a breakdown.

Turning on drilldown as the only way to reach a leaf's value — the group-band zoom button is a SEPARATE affordance from onDatapointClick on purpose; a leaf stays selectable by its own click/Enter without first forcing a reader to drill in.
dataShapes: a nested hierarchy sized by one measure
TreemapChart.avoidWhen: the hierarchy has fewer than 2 levels — a flat bar chart is clearer

UnitChart.purpose: One mark = one honest unit — waffle grid, phyllotaxis field or tick rows, so a share is COUNTED rather than judged by angle or area; lieflat's default replacement for a pie.

stateTokens.marks: fill/stroke resolved per series from the active ChartPalette (--chart-1.. or the mono ladder past 6 series) — never a raw hex
stateTokens.leader: field's cluster-to-label callout is a 0.6px var(--chart-foreground-muted) dashed hairline — furniture, never a second data channel
stateTokens.caption: text-caption in var(--chart-label) for unitLabel, var(--chart-foreground-muted) tabular-nums for the arithmetic remainder
stateTokens.rowValue: rows' value at the inked edge is var(--chart-foreground) at font-weight 800 — the one heavy mark in the row

antiPatterns: Sizing a waffle or field past a few hundred marks in a small frame — one stack stops being countable past ~60 units and here that failure spans the WHOLE canvas, so budget total, columns and frame size together.

Turning showArithmetic off (or padding a count) because a rounded-away caption looks untidy — the caption exists BECAUSE the chart never invents a mark to hit total; hiding it trades the one honest-count promise this chart makes for a tidier footer.

Reaching for layout="field" when the reader needs to rank or compare series precisely — a phyllotaxis cluster reads as an area impression, not a countable structure; a real comparison wants rows or waffle.

Falling back to a pie chart because comparing shares 'still feels easier' — a slice angle cannot be counted, a mark can. If the categories don't sum to a meaningful whole, use the rows layout, not a pie.
dataShapes: parts of a whole as discrete unit counts rather than a percentage, as layout="waffle"
one tally row per category, ticks summing to a total — ticket volume by weekday, for example, as layout="rows"
UnitChart.avoidWhen: exact per-unit counts do not matter — a pie or bar chart reads faster

UnitStack.purpose: n countable marks — rungs, ticks or dots — so a quantity is COUNTED rather than compared; the jitter is seeded, never random.

stateTokens.ink: var(--chart-foreground) unless the caller passes a series token
stateTokens.emphasis: every markEvery-th unit is drawn 1.5x longer and heavier, so the eye counts in fives

antiPatterns: Passing a large n and calling it a bar — past roughly 60 units the stack stops being countable and becomes a texture, at which point a bar is the honest mark. It will happily draw 500; that is your judgment, not its.

Reaching for Math.random to jitter — use seededRnd. Random jitter makes the chart a different picture on every render, so no snapshot, visual-regression shot or play-function assertion can ever agree with itself.
Giving every stack the same seed — neighbouring stacks then jitter in lockstep and the irregularity reads as a pattern, which is worse than no jitter at all. Vary the seed per series or per row.
Turning markEvery off on a long stack — without the every-fifth cue the reader counts one by one, which is exactly the cost this mark was chosen to avoid.

WaterfallChart.purpose: Gross-to-net bridge: running-total steps and subtotal bars showing what added and subtracted along the way.

stateTokens.connector: var(--chart-foreground-muted), 0.6px, dashed (furniture, not data — Leader's default)

antiPatterns: A `total` row whose value does not actually equal the running total at that point — the connector into it visibly plunges/jumps instead of landing flat, which is the bridge silently telling you the reconciliation is wrong.
Reading the dashed connector as if it carries a value — it is furniture that hands off between steps, never a series; the story is the bar heights, not the connector's slope.

Entering a reduction as a positive `value` (or otherwise fighting the sign convention) — color and the +/− label are derived from the actual before/after delta, not from caller intent, so a flipped sign silently mislabels the step.
More than ~6-8 steps in one bridge — past that the running total stops being followable and the connectors turn into visual noise; split into a top-level bridge plus a drill-down instead.
dataShapes: a running total with signed steps into and out of it
WaterfallChart.avoidWhen: there is no meaningful running total — use diverging bars instead

dataShapes: a single value against a target and 2–3 qualitative bands
BulletChart.avoidWhen: more than one value/target pair needs comparing — use a small-multiple row of bullets or a `DumbbellChart`

dataShapes: many overlapping lines over time — one panel per series instead of a spaghetti chart, so each trend reads on its own
one measure across many categories or groups — a grid of panels that share a scale, read as one picture
ChartMultiples.avoidWhen: fewer than 3 panels, or the comparison IS the overlap — use one chart

props.name: value
props.description: The number the bar draws; `null` draws no bar.

props.name: label
props.description: The printed (formatted) value. Always in the accessible tree.

props.name: domain
props.description: `[lo, hi]` of the track; always contains zero (see `barDomain`).

props.name: variant
props.description: `"regular"` (default): bar beside the value; `"slim"`: a thin bar under it.

props.name: track
props.description: Paint the grey remainder of the track.

props.name: fillColor
props.description: A category colour (`var(--chart-N)`) that replaces the positive fill.

props.name: negativeColor
props.description: Paint a negative value in the negative token. Default `true`.

props.name: labelWidth
props.description: Room reserved for the printed value, in `ch` (`labelBoxCh` over the whole column). Every bar in a column then shares one track length, so bar lengths compare down the column and a diverging column's zero rule keeps one x. Unset (or `"slim"`, where the bar sits under the value) leaves the value box to size itself.

props.name: scale
props.description: A categorical scale — its `categories`, in first-seen order.

props.name: title
props.description: What the colours divide the rows BY (the `colorBy` key, or a nicer name).

props.name: formatCategory
props.description: Print a category value; defaults to `String`.

props.name: label
props.description: Trigger label. Defaults to "Columns".

props.name: values
props.type: readonly { key: string; value: number | null }[]
props.description: One entry per row key, in x order; a `null` value draws no column.

props.name: domain
props.description: The value domain: this row's own extent or the column's. Zero is always added.

props.name: label
props.description: Every value as text, for screen readers, sorting and copy.

props.name: height
props.description: Drawing height in px. Default 24.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Render a toolbar above the table; receives the table instance.

props.name: enablePagination
props.description: Enable client-side pagination.

props.name: hidePaginationWhenSingle
props.description: Hide the pager once there's genuinely only one page (`table.getPageCount() <= 1`). Default `true`. When `manualPagination` is set without `rowCount`/`pageCount`, the page count isn't knowable (TanStack falls back to the current page's row count) — in that ambiguous case the pager still renders regardless of this flag, so the existing dev warning (#227) stays the diagnostic instead of a silently-hidden pager. Set to `false` to always show the pager (e.g. while a server total is still loading and you'd rather show a disabled pager than none).

props.name: globalFilter
props.description: Controlled global filter value. When provided, the table reflects this value and the component manages no internal filter state. Keep the source of truth in the app and pass it down — never mutate the filter during render (e.g. `table.setGlobalFilter()` in `toolbar`), which loops.

props.name: onGlobalFilterChange
props.description: Fires when the table requests a global-filter change (e.g. from typeahead).

props.name: sorting
props.description: Controlled sorting state. When provided the component is sorted-controlled.

props.name: columnVisibility
props.description: Controlled column-visibility state.

props.name: columnFilters
props.description: Controlled column-filters state.

props.name: pagination
props.description: Controlled pagination state.

props.name: columnPinning
props.description: Controlled column-pinning state (#333) — the columns frozen against the left and/or right edge while the rest of the table scrolls horizontally. When provided the component is pinning-controlled; otherwise it manages the slice internally and can be seeded once via `initialView.columnPinning`. A pinned column MUST declare an explicit `size` in its `ColumnDef`: the sticky offset is computed from TanStack's `column.getStart("left")` / `getAfter("right")`, which sum the DECLARED sizes, so an auto-width column would render at a width that doesn't match its own offset. A dev-only warning fires for a pinned column with no `size`. Pinning is a LAYOUT concern, not a query concern — it is client-only and never joins `DataTableServerArgs` / `onServerChange`.

props.name: enableColumnResizing
props.description: Opt in to column resizing (#12): a drag handle renders on every resizable column's trailing edge — pointer-draggable (TanStack's own `header.getResizeHandler()`) and keyboard-operable (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight on the focused handle, per the WAI-ARIA separator-as-slider practice). Default `false` so a table that doesn't opt in renders byte-identical markup to before this feature existed — no handle, no per-cell width styling.

props.name: columnResizeMode
props.description: When `columnSizing` updates: `"onChange"` (default here — TanStack's own default is `"onEnd"`) live-updates while dragging; `"onEnd"` updates once on release. Only meaningful when `enableColumnResizing` is set.

props.name: columnSizing
props.description: Controlled column-widths state (#12), keyed by column id — the SAME controlled/uncontrolled shape as `columnPinning`/`rowSelection`. Uncontrolled sizing can be seeded once via `initialView.columnSizing`. A pinned column's sticky offset (`getStart("left")`/`getAfter("right")`) already sums `column.getSize()`, which folds in a `columnSizing` override automatically — so pinning and resizing compose with no extra wiring once this state reaches the table. Sizing is a LAYOUT concern, like `columnPinning`/`rowSelection` — it is client-only and never joins `DataTableServerArgs` / `onServerChange`.

props.name: rowSelection
props.description: Controlled row-selection state (#11) — which rows are checked, keyed by row id (see `getRowId`). When provided the component is selection-controlled; otherwise it manages the slice internally and can be seeded once via `initialView.rowSelection`. Pair it with a selection column built by `createSelectionColumn` (or drive it yourself off the `table` instance handed to `toolbar`). Selection is a LAYOUT/UI concern, not a query concern — like `columnPinning`, it is client-only and never joins `DataTableServerArgs` / `onServerChange`.

props.name: enableRowSelection
props.description: Which rows can be selected: `true`/`false` for all rows, or a predicate evaluated per row. Passed straight through to `useReactTable`. Default (TanStack's own): `true`.

props.name: enableMultiRowSelection
props.description: Allow more than one row to be selected at once. Default (TanStack's own): `true`. Set `false` for single-select (radio-style) behaviour.

props.name: getRowId
props.description: Stable row id, independent of row INDEX. TanStack's default id is set ONCE per row object when the core row model is built, then reused by reference through sorting/filtering — so a client-side sort or filter does NOT disturb selection identity even without this prop. The real hazard is a `data` array replacement: when the app passes NEW object references (a re-fetch, an optimistic update), TanStack rebuilds the core row model from scratch and reassigns default (index-based) ids, so a row that kept its position but got a new object still keeps its selection — but one that MOVED position silently inherits whatever selection belonged to the id now sitting at its old index. This is unavoidable under `manualPagination`: each page IS a fresh `data` array, so the default index-based id restarts at `0` on every page and a selection made on one page can collide with a different record on the next. Supply `getRowId` whenever `data` can be replaced with new object references (including every server-paginated table) so identity survives the replacement instead of falling back to index.

props.name: initialView
props.description: One-shot rehydrate for uncontrolled slices only (ignored for any slice whose corresponding controlled prop is set). Maps to `useReactTable`'s `initialState`.

props.name: manualSorting
props.description: When true, sorting is handled by the server. Pass `sorting` (controlled) and handle `onServerChange` to re-fetch with the new sort params. NOTE: controlled ≠ manual — a controlled `sorting` with `manualSorting:false` still sorts locally.

props.name: manualFiltering
props.description: When true, filtering is handled by the server. NOTE: a controlled `columnFilters` with `manualFiltering:false` still filters locally.

props.name: manualPagination
props.description: When true, pagination is handled by the server.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total row count — used by the server model so TanStack can derive page count. Required when `manualPagination` is true and `pageCount` is not provided.

props.name: pageCount
props.description: Total page count — alternative to `rowCount` for server pagination. When both are provided, `pageCount` wins.

props.name: onServerChange
props.description: Fired after any manual-slice change with the current {pagination, sorting, columnFilters, globalFilter}. The component never fetches; the app must re-fetch and update `data`.

props.name: loading
props.description: When true: overlay spinner; on empty+loading show skeleton rows instead of empty message.

props.name: enableRowVirtualization
props.description: Opt-in to row virtualization (for very large lists). Mutually exclusive with enablePagination in practice — if both are set, virtualization wins: every row stays reachable by scrolling and no pager renders.

props.name: estimateRowHeight
props.description: Estimated row height in px — only the virtualizer's FIRST guess. The table measures its first rendered row and uses that as the estimate from then on, so uniform rows never shift the scroll math. Default: 40.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Fixed row height in px for a virtualized table. Rows are then never measured, which is the fastest path for very large data. Use it only when no row can grow (no wrapping text, markdown or multi-line cells): a taller row still renders fully, but the scrollbar's length drifts.

props.name: overscan
props.description: Virtualizer overscan (rows rendered above/below the visible window). Default: 8.

props.name: maxBodyHeight
props.description: CSS max-height of the scroll container in virtualized mode. Default: "32rem".

props.name: loadingRows
props.description: Number of skeleton placeholder rows to render while loading. Defaults to `pageSize` (non-virtualized) or `min(10, pageSize)` (virtualized).

props.name: zebra
props.description: Gentle alternating row stripes ("zebra") as the row-separation cue, instead of a hairline divider between every row. Default `true` — the stripe is the single separation gesture, so rows carry no divider (a divider on a striped row would be a redundant boundary). Set `false` for the classic line model (a `border-border-strong` divider between rows, no stripes).

props.name: columnDividers
props.description: Draw a quiet `--rule` hairline between columns (header and body). Off by default. Pinned cells keep their own seam and never take a divider.

props.name: layout
props.description: `"table"` (default): always a `<table>`. `"cards"`: always one card per row (a `<dl>` of header → cell). `"auto"`: cards while the table's own container is narrower than 450 px, a `<table>` above. Only the markup changes; sorting, filtering, paging and selection use the same table.

props.name: stickyRows
props.description: Rows pinned to the top or bottom of every page. An "average" or "total" row stays put through sorting, paging and search. Receives each record and its `data` index.

props.name: showRanks
props.description: Prepend a 1…n rank column, in `data` order. Sticky rows are not ranked; the rank travels with its row — sorting never renumbers it.

props.name: rankLabel
props.description: What the rank column is CALLED — its accessible name, its `title`, the term in the cards layout, and the key printed above the table. Defaults to the locale seam (`data.table.rankHeader` / `data.table.rankKey`). The number is the row's position in `data`, not its position on screen, so beside a sorted column it reads 2, 1, 6, 4 on purpose. A column headed by a bare "#" gives a reader no way to know that; this names it.

props.name: density
props.description: `"compact"` tightens row and header height. Default `"default"`.

props.name: mergeEmptyHeaders
props.description: Span an ungrouped column's header over the empty group rows. With grouped headers, the placeholder cells above a column merge into one.

props.name: searchMode
props.description: `"exact"`: a row matches only when a cell equals the query. Default `"contains"` (TanStack's substring search); both ignore case.

props.name: hideHeader
props.description: Hide the header row visually (a pixel heatmap). The headers stay for screen readers, and a focused sort button still shows itself. Sorting is then KEYBOARD-reachable, not clickable: the band has no height, so it offers no hit area — deliberately, since an invisible click target over the first data row would be worse than none. Tab to the column's sort button (it becomes visible on focus) and press Enter.

props.name: enableRowReorder
props.description: Opt-in row drag-reorder. Off by default — an existing table renders byte-identical markup with no extra DOM per row until this is set. Fully controlled like every other slice: the component never mutates `data` itself, it only reports the move via `onRowReorder`; the caller re-orders `data` in response. Keyboard-operable out of the box (`@dnd-kit`'s default keyboard sensor): Space/Enter picks a row up, Arrow Up/Down moves it, Space/Enter drops it, Escape cancels. Every position change is announced through a live region (WCAG 4.1.3). Mutually exclusive with `enableRowVirtualization` — a windowed table can't keep dnd-kit's sortable list and a virtualizer in sync, so reorder is silently disabled (a dev warning fires) when both are set. Combining it with active `sorting` also fires a dev warning (both still work, but a sort re-orders the very rows a drag just moved, which reads as broken). Table-only. The card layout (`layout="cards"`, or `"auto"` at the narrow tier) has no grip column and no row to drop onto, so reorder is a no-op there and `onRowReorder` never fires; a dev warning says so once per mount.

props.name: onRowReorder
props.type: (from: number, to: number, row: TData) => void
props.description: Fires when a row is dropped in a new position. `from`/`to` are indices into the **`data` array you passed in** — never into the sorted, filtered or paginated view the table renders — so they are safe to use directly with `arrayMove`/`slice`+`splice`/immer against your own `data`, unchanged by an active sort or by client-side pagination (the dragged row's true index in the full array, not its index on the current page). Under `manualPagination`, `data` IS the current page, so `from`/`to` are page-relative — reorder that page's own array with them. `row` is the moved record (`data[from]`).

props.name: rowReorderHandle
props.description: Where the drag activator lives. `"cell"` (default) renders a dedicated grip-handle column so the rest of the row keeps its ordinary click/ keyboard behavior untouched. `"row"` makes the whole row itself the drag activator (no extra column) — reach for this only when the row has no other primary interaction (e.g. no `onRowClick`), since a whole-row activator and a row click target the same surface.

props.name: onRowClick
props.description: Fires when a row is activated (#337). Setting it adds ONE activation target per row: a visually-hidden `<button>` rendered inside the row's first cell. That button is the row's keyboard tab stop and its accessible name; a pointer click anywhere else in the row resolves to the same handler, so mouse and keyboard converge on one control instead of two competing ones (a focusable `<tr>` cannot carry an activation role without destroying `row` table semantics). Guarded: a click that originates on a nested interactive control (button/link/input/checkbox/…) or is the tail end of a text-selection drag does NOT fire it. Optional; omitting it renders rows exactly as before.

props.name: rowActionLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the row's hidden activation button (#337). Only read when `onRowClick` is set. Defaults to the row's first visible cell value when that is a string/number (the row's primary identifier — the same naming a link in that cell would get), else the localized `data.table.rowAction` fallback. Supply it whenever the first cell isn't a good name for the row.

props.name: rowClassName
props.description: Per-row className, merged alongside the existing zebra/line/hover/selected classes via `cn()` (so it can't accidentally clobber them) (#337).

props.name: caption
props.description: Accessible name for the table, rendered as a visually-hidden (`sr-only`) `<caption>` — the first child of `<table>`. Screen readers announce it as the table's name and it makes column-header navigation meaningful. Optional; omit it only when the surrounding page already labels the table unambiguously (e.g. an adjacent heading) (#338).

props.name: interaction
props.description: `"table"` (default): a document table — sort buttons and row controls are the tab stops. `"grid"`: the WAI-ARIA grid pattern — ONE tab stop, arrow keys move between header and body cells, Shift / Ctrl(⌘) + click or arrows select cell ranges, Ctrl(⌘)+A selects everything and Ctrl(⌘)+C copies the selection as tab-separated text (what the cells display). Use `DataGrid` for the grid preset.

props.name: enableColumnReorder
props.description: Let people reorder columns by dragging a header (and, in grid mode, with Shift+←/→ on a focused header). Pinned columns reorder within their own pinned block. Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on.

props.name: autoSizeStrategy
props.description: How a grid (`interaction="grid"` with resizing) sizes its columns on its own: `"fit"` scales them to fill the width — on mount and whenever the container resizes — until the user sizes a column themselves; `"content"` auto-sizes every column to its rendered content once, on mount; `"none"` keeps the declared sizes. Default `"none"`; `DataGrid` uses `"fit"`.

props.name: enableColumnMenu
props.description: A per-column options menu in every leaf header: sort, pin, move, auto-size, fit, hide, reset (plus `columnMenuItems`). Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on. In grid mode Alt+↓ on a header opens it.

props.name: columnMenuItems
props.description: Extra entries appended to a column's menu.

props.name: enableContextMenu
props.description: Right-click (Shift+F10) menu on body cells in grid mode: Copy, Copy with headers, Export to CSV, plus `contextMenuItems`. Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on.

props.name: contextMenuItems
props.type: (context: { row: Row<TData>; column: Column<TData, unknown>; cellSelection: DataTableCellSelection; }) => DataTableContextMenuItem[]
props.description: Extra context menu entries for the right-clicked cell.

props.name: exportFileName
props.description: File name (without extension) for "Export to CSV". Default `"export"`.

props.name: showStatusBar
props.description: A status bar under the table: row / filtered / selected counts and, in grid mode, Count / Sum / Average / Min / Max of the selected range. Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on.

props.name: enableFilterUI
props.description: A filter button in every filterable leaf header, opening the column's filter panel: text / number / date conditions (two, joined by AND / OR, dates with relative ranges such as "Last 30 days"), a checklist of the column's values with counts and search (`set`), or yes / no. The kind comes from `meta.filter`, else from the data. Filters are plain JSON models in the `columnFilters` slice, so views and agents can save and set them. Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on.

props.name: floatingFilters
props.description: A row under the headers with a filter field per column: type to filter a text column, `>100`, `<=5`, `!=0` or `10..20` in a number column; other kinds show their summary and open the panel. Requires `enableFilterUI`.

props.name: showFilterChips
props.description: Chips above the table naming every active column filter ("Region: EU, US"), each removable, plus Clear all. Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on.

props.name: enableFind
props.description: Grid mode: Ctrl/⌘+F inside the grid opens a find bar that searches every row the grid holds (after filters, rendered or not) in the text the cells display, counts the matching cells, steps through them with Enter / Shift+Enter (moving the active cell) and highlights them. Default `false`; `DataGrid` turns it on.

props.name: columnOrder
props.description: Controlled column order (leaf column ids).

props.name: cellSelection
props.description: Controlled cell ranges (`interaction="grid"`).

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Message shown when there are no rows and not loading.

props.name: lead
props.description: Content above the fields (the selection checkbox, the rank, the row action).

props.name: density
props.description: `compact` tightens the padding, like the table's `density="compact"`.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's accessible NAME, and its `title`. Defaults to the locale seam's `data.table.rankHeader`. The visible glyph stays "#" — it has to, in a 40px column — so the glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and this string is what the column is actually called. Without it the header's accessible name is the single character "#", which says nothing about WHICH position is printed: beside a sorted column the numbers legitimately read 2, 1, 6, 4 and a reader has no way to learn why. `DataTable` prints the same rule visibly, once, above the table (`data-slot="data-table-rank-key"`).

props.name: selected
props.description: Currently selected values (controlled).

props.name: children
props.description: Left cluster: search + facet filters.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right cluster: column picker, export, primary actions.

props.name: label
props.description: Label-in-value text — `"Status: Failed"`, never `"Status = failed"` and never a bare `"Failed"`. Same contract as the base `FilterChip`.

props.name: count
props.description: How many records this active filter excluded (or matched) — rendered as a secondary, locale-formatted segment alongside `label`. Omit for a bare chip with no count.

props.name: countLabel
props.description: The word placed before the formatted count, e.g. `"excluded"` → `"excluded 1,204"`. Omitted by default: a bare `count` renders as just the formatted number.

props.name: label
props.description: The printed (formatted) value. Always in the accessible tree.

props.name: hideValue
props.description: Hide the value visually; it stays for screen readers, sorting and copy.

props.name: title
props.description: What the colours measure (the column's header).

props.name: images
props.description: Render `![alt](src)` as an image. Default `false` (the alt text prints).

props.name: label
props.description: Visually-hidden accessible label. Defaults to the localized "Search" microcopy.

props.name: domain
props.description: The y domain: this row's own extent (`range: "cell"`) or the column's.

props.name: label
props.description: Every value as text, for screen readers, sorting and copy.

props.name: ends
props.description: Printed first / last values (with `labels: "ends"`).

props.name: endsWidth
props.description: Room reserved for those two labels, in `ch` (`labelBoxCh` over the whole column). The drawing takes what they leave over, so one reservation per column keeps every row's line on the same x scale.

props.name: height
props.description: Drawing height in px. Default 24.

DataTable.purpose: TanStack-backed data grid with sorting, filtering, pagination and a render-prop toolbar.

stateTokens.rowHover: hover:bg-foreground/10 (a foreground-tint wash, so it beats the zebra stripe in the same direction on light AND dark)
stateTokens.header: bg-surface-muted when sticky, else bg-surface-muted/60 + border-b border-border-strong (the header bottom is the SOLE cue between header and first row → the strong rung, #173)
stateTokens.rowDivider: zebra={false}: border-b border-border-strong last:border-b-0; zebra rows use bg-table-stripe instead (the stripe replaces the divider)

antiPatterns: Forking table state into the toolbar — pass the table instance via toolbar={(table) => …}; don't duplicate sorting/filter state.
Hand-rolling virtualization for >50 rows — the DataTable owns it.
Status cells as raw colored text — render a Badge so it reads in every theme.
Decorating a dense table with callouts/hatch — decoration density goes DOWN as information density goes UP.

SearchInput.purpose: Controlled search box that drives a DataTable's global filter.

stateTokens.focus: focus-ring — the compound indicator: a ring-2 in --ring plus a 1px --ring-contour outline (#67)

antiPatterns: Keeping uncontrolled internal state — SearchInput is controlled (value + onChange); reflect filter state into the table.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled content. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial content for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires on every edit with the full document text.

props.name: language
props.description: Monaco language id (e.g. "typescript", "json"). Defaults to "typescript".

props.name: path
props.description: Model path/URI — drives per-file language services + diagnostics.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Render the editor read-only.

props.name: height
props.description: Editor height. Number → px. Defaults to "100%" (size via the parent).

props.name: options
props.description: Passthrough Monaco construction options (merged over the defaults).

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the editor. Maps onto Monaco's `ariaLabel` construction option AND the inner screen-reader `<textarea>` (`aria-label`), so assistive tech announces a name. Spreading `aria-label` via `...props` only lands on the wrapper div and never reaches Monaco's focusable textarea — use this instead.

props.name: ariaInvalid
props.description: Sets `aria-invalid` on Monaco's inner `<textarea>` to convey validity.

props.name: ariaDescribedBy
props.description: Sets `aria-describedby` on Monaco's inner `<textarea>` (e.g. an error id).

props.name: contextMenu
props.description: Right-click menu. `"brand"` (default) replaces Monaco's built-in menu with brand-ui's `ContextMenu`; `"monaco"` keeps Monaco's themed menu; `"none"` disables it.

props.name: onMount
props.description: Called once the editor instance + monaco namespace are ready.

props.name: actions
props.description: Declarative Monaco editor actions — each registers a command (run on its `keybindings`, in the command palette, and optionally the context menu via `contextMenuGroupId`). Wraps `editor.addAction`; re-registered when the array identity changes, disposed on unmount. Build keybindings with the re-exported `monaco` namespace, e.g. `keybindings: [monaco.KeyMod.CtrlCmd | monaco.KeyCode.Slash]`. Note: a context-menu entry only shows when `contextMenu="monaco"`, but the keybinding and command palette work regardless. Memoize `actions` to avoid re-registering on every render.

props.name: files
props.description: Open files, one tab each.

props.name: activePath
props.description: Controlled active file path.

props.name: defaultActivePath
props.description: Initial active path for uncontrolled use. Defaults to the first file.

props.name: onActivePathChange
props.description: Called when the active tab changes.

props.name: onFileChange
props.description: Called on every edit with the file path + new content.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Render all files read-only.

props.name: height
props.description: Workspace height. Number → px. Defaults to "100%".

props.name: value
props.description: Text written to the clipboard on click.

props.name: label
props.description: Show the "Copy" / "Copied" label next to the icon. Defaults to true.

props.name: original
props.description: Left/original document.

props.name: modified
props.description: Right/modified document.

props.name: language
props.description: Monaco language id applied to both sides. Defaults to "typescript".

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Read-only (diffs are read-only by default).

props.name: renderSideBySide
props.description: Side-by-side (true) vs inline (false) diff. Defaults to side-by-side.

props.name: height
props.description: Editor height. Number → px. Defaults to "100%".

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the diff. Each side is a Monaco editor with its own focusable screen-reader surface, so both get the name, suffixed " (original)" / " (modified)" — without it axe reports `aria-input-field-name` on both sides. Maps onto Monaco's `originalAriaLabel`/`modifiedAriaLabel` diff options, and is re-sent with every option update the component makes (Monaco resets both names on any update that omits them).

props.name: options
props.description: Passthrough Monaco diff options (merged over the defaults).

props.name: onMount
props.description: Called once the diff editor + monaco namespace are ready.

props.name: editor
props.description: The Monaco editor instance to act on (null until mounted).

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Hide editing items (cut/paste/format) for read-only editors.

props.name: children
props.description: The editor element wrapped as the right-click trigger.

props.name: filename
props.description: Filename shown on the left (e.g. "index.ts").

props.name: language
props.description: Active language id; shows a language picker when `onLanguageChange` is set.

props.name: onLanguageChange
props.description: Called when the user picks a language. Omit to hide the picker.

props.name: languages
props.description: Languages offered in the picker. Defaults to {@link EDITOR_LANGUAGES}.

props.name: copyValue
props.description: Text copied by the copy button. Omit to hide the button.

props.name: actions
props.description: Extra actions rendered before the copy button (brand-ui buttons, etc.).

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled markdown value. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial markdown for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires on every edit with the full markdown document.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Render the editor read-only (still selectable, not editable).

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the editable surface. Milkdown/ProseMirror renders an ARIA `textbox` (`contenteditable`); without a name, screen readers announce an unlabeled field. Set onto the ProseMirror view's `attributes`. Default `"Markdown editor"`.

props.name: slashMenu
props.type: boolean | { commands?: SlashCommand[]; trigger?: string; shortcut?: string }
props.description: Enable the `/` command menu (insert brand `:::` directives + basic blocks live at the caret). `true` (default) uses the built-in {@link BRAND_SLASH_COMMANDS}; pass a `commands` array to extend/replace them, or `false` to disable. The `trigger` defaults to `"/"`. Pass `shortcut` (default `"Mod-Shift-O"`) to control the keyboard shortcut that opens the menu at the caret without typing the trigger character — works in BOTH the WYSIWYG pane and the Monaco source pane (#271).

props.name: calc
props.description: Opt-in calc authoring inside ```calc fences (off by default). Supply the consumer's hooks — `tokenize` (highlight), `evaluate` (result inlays), and/or `complete` (autocomplete; Monaco surface). The library DECORATES, the consumer COMPUTES — no calc engine is bundled. Mirrors `MarkdownPreview`'s `evaluate`.

props.name: completions
props.description: Declarative completion providers (#283) — e.g. `[[wikilink]]` autocomplete. Off by default; mirrors the `slashMenu`/`calc` opt-in pattern. Each provider registers a `triggerCharacters` set + a `provide(ctx)` that returns candidates; the library owns detecting the trigger and rendering/inserting. This is a DELIBERATELY MINIMAL, best-effort mirror of the Monaco source-pane behavior (see `markdown-editor/completions/completions-prose.ts` for the exact gaps — no real cross-block line/column, a plain listbox instead of a native suggest widget). Forwarded from `MarkdownWorkspace`'s `completions` prop, which also wires the FULL Monaco/source-pane path.

props.name: onEmbedAsset
props.description: Host-provided callback for image paste/drop embedding. When set, the editor intercepts paste and drop events that contain image files, shows an inline "uploading…" placeholder, calls this function with the `File`, and on resolve inserts `![filename](returnedPath)` in the document. On reject the placeholder is removed and an inline error chip (+ toast) is shown — the document never contains a broken image. If not set, the editor's default paste/drop behavior is unchanged. The library NEVER stores assets — all persistence is the host's responsibility.

CalcBlock.purpose: A live calculation block inside markdown: inputs, a formula and its result, recomputed as the inputs change.

CalcInline.purpose: An inline calculated value inside prose that updates with the document's variables.

CodeEditor.purpose: Monaco-backed editable code editor (controlled/uncontrolled), themed from tokens.
antiPatterns: Passing Monaco a hardcoded theme — the bridge reads the active data-theme tokens; never override it.
Using CodeEditor for read-only display — use CodeBlock (@elabs-ai/components-ai, Shiki) for non-editable code.
Forgetting the worker setup (import "@elabs-ai/components-editor/monaco-environment") — IntelliSense is off without it.

DecisionCard.purpose: An agent's decision presented as a card in the document — the option taken, the alternatives and the rationale — for the reader to accept or revise.

DiffEditor.purpose: The Monaco side-by-side diff surface — the only diff in the library that can be typed into.

avoidNextTo: DiffView

antiPatterns: Reaching for it to READ a patch — that is DiffView in @elabs-ai/components-ai, which needs no editor engine at all.
Reaching for it to approve or reject hunks — that is ChangeReview, which owns the trust gate.
Rendering it in a jsdom unit test — it is Monaco; test the surrounding wiring and leave the editor to a browser story.

DocumentOutline.purpose: The heading outline of a document as a navigable tree that scrolls the editor to the chosen section.

IterationBuilderDialog.purpose: A dialog for composing a document iteration: pick the sections to keep, add and rework, then apply.

IterationTemplateDialog.purpose: A dialog for starting a document from a template, with the template's fields filled in before insertion.

MarkdownWorkspace.purpose: A markdown editing workspace: the editor with its outline, preview and toolbar arranged as one document surface.

MermaidDiagram.purpose: A diagram rendered from Mermaid source, themed with the design tokens and readable in both themes.

MermaidWorkspace.purpose: Mermaid source beside its rendered diagram, with the preview updating as the source changes.

props.name: background
props.description: Render a branded dotted background grid. Defaults to true.

props.name: helperLines
props.description: Enable alignment guides + snapping while a single node is dragged. Off by default; when false, CanvasShell behaves exactly as before. When true, CanvasShell wires `useHelperLines` around your `onNodesChange` and renders the `<HelperLines>` overlay internally — pass `nodes` + `onNodesChange` (the standard controlled setup, e.g. via `useNodesState`). For full control use the exported `useHelperLines` + `<HelperLines>` directly.

props.name: fitViewKey
props.description: Re-fit the viewport whenever this value changes. React Flow's own `fitView` prop fits ONCE, as soon as the nodes are first measured, and then never again. A canvas whose positions arrive AFTER that first paint — anything laid out asynchronously, e.g. a debounced `layoutFlow` pass — therefore gets fitted to the pre-layout positions (typically every node still stacked at the origin) and stays there. Measured on the process map: the viewport pinned at React Flow's `maxZoom` of 2 with 2 of 11 nodes on screen, while the layout underneath was correct the whole time. Pass the key the layout is cached on (structure + direction), NOT something that changes on every render and not a metric: a re-fit is a viewport jump, so it must happen when the picture genuinely moved and never while the reader is reading. The fit waits for `useNodesInitialized`, so it measures real node boxes rather than fitting a degenerate bounding box a second time.

props.name: fitViewKeyOptions
props.description: Options for the {@link fitViewKey} re-fit. Ignored without one.

props.name: fitViewAnchorNodeIds
props.description: Which nodes a CLAMPED {@link fitViewKey} re-fit keeps in view — typically where the diagram begins. A fit that cannot shrink far enough (a `minZoom` floor) is pinned to the content's top-left corner by default, which is where a top-down layout starts; a left-to-right layout starts at the left edge but at mid-height, so pinning to the top opens on an empty corner. With anchors, each overflowing axis centres the anchor nodes instead, without ever scrolling past the content's own edge. Unset: today's corner pin.

props.name: children
props.description: Overlays rendered inside the flow (ZoomControls, Legend, Panels).

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label, e.g. a frequency count ("128×").

props.name: secondaryLabel
props.description: Secondary label rendered alongside the primary, e.g. a duration ("3.4d avg").

props.name: x
props.description: Label anchor, from `getBezierPath`/`getSmoothStepPath`'s `labelX`/`labelY`.

props.name: selected
props.description: Matches the parent edge's `selected` state.

props.name: path
props.description: SVG path `d` for this edge, from `getBezierPath`/`getSmoothStepPath`/…

props.name: stroke
props.description: Resting stroke paint — a `var(--token)` reference or a resolved colour.

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Resting stroke width in px. The focus layers are drawn wider than this.

props.name: strokeDasharray
props.description: Dash pattern, applied to the edge AND to both focus layers so a dashed edge keeps its shape when focused.

props.name: strokeOpacity
props.description: Stroke opacity for the edge itself. Never applied to the focus layers.

props.name: markerEnd
props.description: React Flow marker url, e.g. from `EdgeProps.markerEnd`.

props.name: markerStart
props.description: React Flow marker url, e.g. from `EdgeProps.markerStart`.

props.name: interactionWidth
props.description: Width of the invisible pointer-target path React Flow draws over the edge.

props.name: style
props.description: Merged onto the edge path, last — so a consumer's `style.stroke` still wins.

props.name: path
props.description: SVG path `d` the tokens travel along — the same string the edge draws.

props.name: tokens
props.description: Tokens to place. The parent owns `progress`; this part keeps no clock.

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Absolute flow-y of the horizontal guide (from `useHelperLines`).

props.name: vertical
props.description: Absolute flow-x of the vertical guide (from `useHelperLines`).

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Empty-state shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: hasSelection
props.description: When false, render the empty state instead of children.

props.name: selectionKey
props.description: Stable identity of the current selection (e.g. the selected node's id). When it changes, the body replays a quick fade so it reads as "details for THIS node". Pass the selected entity's id (or any stable key derived from the selected data).

props.name: open
props.description: Collapse (research 09 step 3 — converged on the shared `@elabs-ai/components-ui` `useCollapsiblePanel` base; the panel stays single-view, drill-in is ContextPanel-only). Controlled `open` / uncontrolled `defaultOpen`.

props.name: side
props.description: Which edge the panel sits on (collapse slide direction). Default `"right"`.

props.name: width
props.description: Expanded width (any CSS length). Default `"18rem"` (the original `w-72`).

CanvasShell.purpose: Branded React Flow canvas wrapper with token-driven background + sane defaults.
antiPatterns: Hardcoding node/edge colors — use the flow-node/flow-edge tokens so the canvas matches the theme.
Hiding the React Flow attribution without the appropriate license.
Forgetting to import @xyflow/react/dist/style.css once in the consuming app.

Controls.purpose: Zoom / fit / lock controls for the agent workspace Canvas.

stateTokens.surface: bg-card + rounded-md border (a raised control cluster over the canvas)

antiPatterns: Building a second zoom control in a Panel — one control cluster per canvas, or the two disagree.
Dropping the keyboard path — every canvas action must stay reachable without a pointer.
Stacking it under the canvas content — it is chrome and must stay above the graph and clickable.
Raw colors on the node — use flow-node tokens.

NodeToolbar.purpose: The contextual action bar attached to a selected workspace-graph node.
antiPatterns: Using it as the canvas-wide toolbar — it is a NODE toolbar and is positioned against the selected node.
Reaching for it when you want the WAI-ARIA keyboard toolbar — that is Toolbar in @elabs-ai/components-ui.
Putting destructive node actions in it with no confirm/undo — deleting a node loses its edges too.
Filling it with icon-only buttons and no labels — every icon-only control needs an accessible name.

Panel.purpose: A floating overlay panel pinned to a corner of the workspace Canvas.

stateTokens.surface: bg-card + rounded-md border (raised above the canvas ground)

antiPatterns: Using it as the app's side rail — that is ContextPanel; this floats over the graph.
Filling a corner panel with a long scrollable list — it overlays the graph the user is trying to read.
Stacking several panels in one corner — they occlude each other; give each corner one job.

props.name: morph
props.description: - `"auto"` (default): renders the full lockup (glyph + wordmark) and **morphs to the glyph alone when inside a collapsed `Sidebar`** (`group-data-[collapsible=icon]`) — a crossfade + width transition. Outside a collapsible sidebar it just shows the lockup. - `"mark"` / `"lockup"`: force a fixed variant (no morph).

props.name: height
props.description: Rendered height in px. Width scales with the variant. Default 24.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color treatment, forwarded to `BrandLogo`. "auto" reads the per-theme brand tokens.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name, and the wordmark rendered in the lockup. Default "Brand".

props.name: variant
props.description: "mark" = the circle-and-square glyph only; "lockup" = glyph + wordmark. Defaults to "lockup".

props.name: height
props.description: Rendered height in px. Width scales with the variant. Defaults to 28.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color treatment. "auto" (default) reads the per-theme brand-mark tokens, so the mark takes the active theme's approved colorway. "white" forces the fully-white mark for placing ON a colored surface (a primary button, a dark brand chip).

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name — AND, in the `lockup` variant, the wordmark that is rendered beside the glyph. Defaults to "Brand". This is the seam that makes the logo unbranded: a consumer passes their own name and gets their own lockup, with no SVG path data to edit. The glyph itself is the only fixed part.

props.name: size
props.description: Pixel size for both width & height. Defaults to 24.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name. When provided the icon is exposed to AT as an image; when omitted the icon is treated as decorative (aria-hidden).

props.name: variant
props.description: Force the outline or solid glyph, overriding the theme's `--icon-fill` token. Only icons created with `createIcon`'s `solid` option have a solid glyph to switch to — every other icon renders outline regardless of this prop. `Icon` used directly with raw `children` ignores it (it has no separate solid content to switch to).

props.name: name
props.description: The service's registry key, e.g. "slack", "github". An unregistered name renders a monogram fallback instead of broken/blank output.

props.name: size
props.description: Pixel size for both width & height. Defaults to 24 (mirrors `Icon`).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name override. Defaults to the registry entry's own `label`, else a title-cased `name`. Ignored when `decorative` is set.

props.name: variant
props.description: "brand" (default) renders the mark's own colours. "mono" asks a registered `render` mark to draw via `currentColor` (best-effort — it's the mark author's choice) and desaturates a `src` image; the fallback tile is already mono regardless of this prop.

props.name: logos
props.description: Scope marks to this instance only, merged over (and overriding) the global registry — for tests or a locally-scoped set.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Set true when adjacent visible text already names the service, so the mark is hidden from assistive tech instead of announcing a duplicate name. Defaults to false — the mark carries its own accessible name.

AppIcon.purpose: The standard app/brand mark for app chrome — theme-aware, morphs mark↔lockup on sidebar collapse.
antiPatterns: Hand-rolling BrandLogo plus a lucide box in app chrome — AppIcon is the standard app mark.
Using AppIcon as a brand-neutral scaffold placeholder or a multi-tenant team switcher — it is the product's own mark.

BrandLogo.purpose: The product's mark/lockup, drawn from tokens so it adapts to every theme.
antiPatterns: Hardcoding a brand fill — the mark uses currentColor/tokens so it adapts per theme.
Hand-rolling the mark↔lockup swap in app chrome — AppIcon wraps BrandLogo and morphs on sidebar collapse.

DashboardIcon.purpose: The product-vocabulary icon set: brand and domain glyphs built on the shared icon primitive.

Icon.purpose: The brand/product-vocabulary icon primitive — 24×24, stroke = currentColor, so it themes with text.
antiPatterns: Reaching here for a generic glyph (chevron, close, search, menu) — those come from lucide-react.
A meaning-bearing icon with no title — an untitled Icon is decorative and hidden from assistive tech by design.
A raw color on an icon — it inherits currentColor so it adapts per theme.

props.name: longitude
props.description: Longitude of the point the note is about.

props.name: latitude
props.description: Latitude of the point the note is about.

props.name: text
props.description: The note. Plain text reads best; it moves into the key at `narrow`.

props.name: anchor
props.description: Where the text sits relative to the point (default `"top-right"`).

props.name: connector
props.description: The leader line from the point to the text (default: a plain line). Pass `false` to set the text right beside the point with no line.

props.name: showAt
props.description: Whether the note shows at a tier (default `true` everywhere). A hidden note takes no number, so the key stays gap-free.

props.name: priority
props.description: Paint order among annotations: a higher one paints on top (0–8, default 0).

props.name: rows
props.description: The rows, in reading order.

props.name: data
props.description: Array of arcs to render. Each arc must have a unique `id`.

props.name: id
props.description: Optional unique identifier prefix for the arc source/layers. Auto-generated if not provided.

props.name: curvature
props.description: How far each arc bows away from a straight line. `0` renders straight lines; higher values bend further; negative values bend to the opposite side. Arcs cross the antimeridian via the shorter direction. (default: 0.2)

props.name: samples
props.description: Number of samples used to render each curve. Higher = smoother. (default: 64)

props.name: paint
props.description: MapLibre paint properties for the arc layer. Merged on top of theme-aware defaults (`line-color` = the `--primary` token, `line-width: 2`, `line-opacity: 0.85`). Any value can be a MapLibre expression for per-feature styling; every field on each arc datum (besides `from`/`to`) is exposed via `["get", ...]`.

props.name: layout
props.description: MapLibre layout properties for the arc layer. Defaults to rounded joins/caps.

props.name: hoverPaint
props.description: Paint properties applied to the arc currently under the cursor. Each key is merged into `paint` as a `case` expression keyed on per-feature hover state, so only the hovered arc changes appearance.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when an arc is clicked.

props.name: onHover
props.description: Callback fired when the hovered arc changes. Receives the cursor's lng/lat at the moment of entry, and `null` when the cursor leaves the last hovered arc.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Whether arcs respond to mouse events (default: true).

props.name: beforeId
props.description: Optional MapLibre layer id to insert the arc layers before (z-order control).

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the map container.

props.name: theme
props.description: Basemap flavor. If not provided, it is derived from the active brand theme (`data-theme` + that theme's own `color-scheme`), then a `dark`/`light` root class, then the OS preference.

props.name: styles
props.description: Custom map styles for light and dark themes. Overrides the default Carto styles.

props.name: blank
props.description: Use a transparent, tile-less basemap instead of the default Carto street basemap — a blank canvas. Used alone it renders nothing; add your own layers on top (`<MapGeoJSON>`, `<MapArc>`, markers, …). Ideal for data visualizations. Ignored when an explicit `styles` prop is provided.

props.name: basemapLabels
props.description: Draw the basemap's own place labels. `false` leaves the ground and hides every text label the basemap style carries, so the map's own labels (`MapMarker`'s `label`, `MapAnnotation`) are the only naming on it — the locator recipe, and the default inside `MapInset`, where a full-size label is sliced by the frame. Default `true`.

props.name: projection
props.description: Map projection: `"mercator"` (MapLibre's default) or `"globe"` for a 3D globe view, or a full MapLibre projection spec. Feature-detected: a MapLibre build that cannot switch projections ignores it (with a console note).

props.name: interactive
props.description: `false` makes the map STATIC — the editorial / locator default: no zoom, pan, rotate or keyboard handlers, the default cursor and no tab stop (leave `<MapControls>` out of a static map). Hover and click still reach layers and markers, so tooltips keep working. The viewport can still be set in code (`viewport`, the ref). Default `true`.

props.name: height
props.description: The map's height: CSS px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per tier — `{ base: { aspect: 1.6 }, narrow: { aspect: 1 } }`. Tiers are measured on the map's own width (`narrow` < 480 px, `medium` < 768 px). Unset, the map fills its parent as before; a parent with no height of its own gets `DEFAULT_MAP_HEIGHT` (1.6 : 1, square at `narrow`) instead of 0.

props.name: viewport
props.description: Controlled viewport. When provided together with `onViewportChange`, the map becomes controlled and the viewport is driven by this prop.

props.name: onViewportChange
props.description: Callback fired continuously as the viewport changes (pan, zoom, rotate, pitch). Use standalone to observe changes, or with `viewport` for controlled mode.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a loading overlay on the map (e.g. while the app fetches map data).

props.name: plan
props.description: Turn the canvas into a CUSTOM (non-geographic) plan map: a floor plan, a factory layout, a train carriage, a rack elevation. Pass the plan's extent (`{ width, height }` in the plan's own units) or a `createPlanCrs(…)` result, and every layer inside then speaks PLAN coordinates instead of lng/lat — shapes, routes, markers and popups alike. The plan is fitted on mount, pan and zoom are clamped to its extent, and rotation and pitch are off (a rotated floor plan is unreadable). Pair it with `blank` and, for a picture under the shapes, `<MapPlanImage>`. The plan coordinate system is synthesized on Web Mercator, so it is not a georeference: distances belong to the plan, and a scale bar would lie.

props.name: fitPlan
props.description: Fit a plan map to its extent on mount and whenever the extent changes (default: true). Ignored on a geographic map, and skipped when the camera is driven through `viewport`.

props.name: data
props.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection data or a URL to fetch GeoJSON from.

props.name: clusterMaxZoom
props.description: Maximum zoom level to cluster points on (default: 14).

props.name: clusterRadius
props.description: Radius of each cluster when clustering points, in pixels (default: 50).

props.name: clusterColors
props.description: Colors for cluster circles: [small, medium, large] based on point count. Defaults to the theme's `--success`/`--warning`/`--destructive` tokens.

props.name: clusterThresholds
props.description: Point-count thresholds for the color/size steps: [medium, large] (default: [100, 750]).

props.name: pointColor
props.description: Color for unclustered individual points. Defaults to the theme's `--primary` token.

props.name: onPointClick
props.type: ( feature: GeoJSON.Feature<GeoJSON.Point, P>, coordinates: [number, number], ) => void
props.description: Callback when an unclustered point is clicked.

props.name: onClusterClick
props.type: (clusterId: number, coordinates: [number, number], pointCount: number) => void
props.description: Callback when a cluster is clicked. If not provided, zooms into the cluster.

props.name: position
props.description: Position of the controls on the map (default: "bottom-right").

props.name: showZoom
props.description: Show zoom in/out buttons. Default: true on an interactive map, false on a static one (`<MapCanvas interactive={false}>`), whose whole point is a fixed view — set `showZoom` explicitly to override either way.

props.name: showCompass
props.description: Show a compass button to reset bearing/pitch (default: false).

props.name: showLocate
props.description: Show a locate button to fly to the user's location (default: false).

props.name: showFullscreen
props.description: Show a fullscreen toggle button (default: false).

props.name: showFit
props.description: Show a button that frames the whole plan again — a plan map has an edge to come back to, so this defaults to ON there and off on a geographic map.

props.name: fitBounds
props.description: What the fit button frames. Defaults to the plan's own extent; pass bounds to frame something else (one wing, the selected cluster).

props.name: onFit
props.description: Called after the camera has been asked to frame the plan.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the controls container.

props.name: onLocate
props.description: Callback with user coordinates when located.

props.name: onLocateError
props.description: Callback when geolocation fails or is denied.

props.name: data
props.description: GeoJSON data (FeatureCollection, Feature, Geometry) or a URL to fetch it from. On a canvas with a `plan` extent the coordinates are PLAN units — `[x, y]` in the plan's own drawing units — and are converted for you.

props.name: id
props.description: Optional unique identifier prefix for the source/layers. Auto-generated if not provided.

props.name: promoteId
props.description: Feature property to promote to the feature `id`. Required for hover and selected feature-state (`fillHoverPaint`, `selectedId`) and stable `onHover`/`onClick` payloads.

props.name: fillPaint
props.description: Paint for the polygon fill layer. Merged on top of a theme-aware neutral default (the `--border` token — a mid neutral that reads on the page surface in every theme). Pass `false` to omit the fill layer entirely (e.g. outlines only).

props.name: linePaint
props.description: Paint for the outline layer. Merged on top of a hairline default (`line-color` = the `--background` token, `line-width` = 0.5) for thin separators. Override `line-color` if your container differs, or pass `false` to omit the layer.

props.name: fillHoverPaint
props.description: Paint merged onto the fill layer for the feature under the cursor, applied as a `case` expression keyed on hover feature-state. Requires `promoteId`.

props.name: fillOpacity
props.description: The fill layer's opacity, 0–1 — shorthand for `fillPaint["fill-opacity"]` (which wins when both are set). Default 1, or 0.25 with a `pattern`, so the stripes read over a tint of the same colour.

props.name: pattern
props.description: Hatch the areas with stripes (see {@link MapGeoJSONPattern}).

props.name: vignette
props.description: Glow around the areas' edges (see {@link MapGeoJSONVignette}).

props.name: lineHoverPaint
props.description: The outline equivalent of `fillHoverPaint`. Requires `promoteId`.

props.name: fillSelectedPaint
props.description: Paint merged onto the fill layer for the feature(s) named by `selectedId`. Applied outside hover, so a selected feature still looks selected while the cursor is over it. Requires `promoteId`.

props.name: lineSelectedPaint
props.description: The outline equivalent of `fillSelectedPaint`. Requires `promoteId`.

props.name: selectedId
props.description: The selected feature id(s) — the promoted `promoteId` values. Selection is the consumer's state; this only paints it.

props.name: hoveredId
props.description: Take over the highlight: when set, the hover paint follows THIS id instead of the pointer. That is how `MapPlanOverlay` makes a keyboard-focused room light up exactly as a hovered one does — one channel, one appearance.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when a feature is clicked.

props.name: onHover
props.description: Callback fired when the hovered feature changes; `null` when the cursor leaves.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Whether features respond to mouse events. Defaults to `false` on a geographic canvas and `true` on a plan canvas, where the shapes ARE the subject rather than a backdrop.

props.name: featureLabel
props.description: The text of a feature in the keyboard list an `interactive` map renders — one visually-hidden button per feature, so the values a pointer reveals on hover are reachable by Tab and readable by a screen reader (WCAG 2.1.1 and 1.3.1). Say what the region is AND what it is worth — the same sentence a hover readout prints. Defaults to the promoted id.

props.name: pickPadding
